Your company has an Azure AD tenant that includes a user named User1.  
  
The company has two departments: marketing and finance.  
  
You need to grant User1 permission to manage only users in the marketing department. The solution must ensure that User1 does **NOT** have permission to manage users in the finance department.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
An administrative unit scopes Microsoft Entra directory-role permissions to a defined subset of the organization. Placing marketing users in an administrative unit and assigning User1 an appropriate role at that administrative-unit scope permits management of those users without granting equivalent permissions over finance users outside the unit.

**Learn more:** [Administrative units in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/administrative-units) · [Assign Microsoft Entra roles with administrative unit scope](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/manage-roles-portal)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An Azure AD tenant has multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforced and self-service password reset (SSPR) enabled.  
  
Combined registration is enabled in interrupt mode.  
  
A new user named User1 is created.  
  
Which two authentication methods can User1 use to finish the combined registration process? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Combined registration applies both the MFA and SSPR policies. Microsoft Authenticator is registerable and supports MFA and SSPR, while email is a registerable SSPR method that can be selected as the additional registration method. FIDO2 security keys are MFA methods rather than SSPR methods; hardware tokens cannot be registered in the combined-registration flow; and Windows Hello for Business is registered through Windows setup or Settings.

**Learn more:** [Combined registration for SSPR and Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-registration-mfa-sspr-combined) · [Microsoft Entra authentication overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/overview-authentication)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You are assessing enterprise software-as-a-service (SaaS) apps.  
  
You must ensure that the apps support automatic provisioning of Azure AD users.  
  
Which specification must the apps support?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID uses the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) 2.0 protocol to automatically create, update, synchronize, and deprovision users in SaaS applications through a SCIM user-management API endpoint.\
\
**Learn more:** [How Application Provisioning works in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/app-provisioning/how-provisioning-works) · [SCIM support in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/app-provisioning/scim-support-in-entra-id)

options.text: the Conditional Access What If tool
sign-ins logs in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)
the activity logs in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
access reviews in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)

questions.explanation:
The Conditional Access What If tool simulates a sign-in with specified conditions and reports which Conditional Access policies apply. Its evaluation supports both location/country and a high sign-in-risk level, allowing the policy’s block outcome to be tested without requiring an actual risky sign-in.

**Learn more:** [The Conditional Access What If tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/what-if-tool) · [What If evaluation - Microsoft Graph v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-evaluate?view=graph-rest-1.0)

Your company has two divisions, named Contoso East and Contoso West. The Microsoft 365 identity architecture for the two divisions is shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708092268-kz9kda2x.jpg)  
  
You need to grant users in the Contoso East division access to Microsoft SharePoint Online sites in the Contoso West tenant. The solution must not require any additional Microsoft 365 licenses.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure Azure AD Application Proxy in the Contoso West tenant.
Invite the Contoso East users as guests in the Contoso West tenant.
Deploy a second Azure AD Connect server to Contoso East and configure the server to sync the Contoso East Active Directory forest to the Contoso West tenant.
Configure the existing Azure AD Connect server in Contoso East to sync the Contoso East Active Directory forest to the Contoso West tenant.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration lets a resource tenant invite users from another organization as guest users and authorize them for SharePoint Online resources. The guest users authenticate by using their home-tenant identities, while Contoso West controls their access; this avoids provisioning duplicate synchronized users or assigning additional Microsoft 365 licenses in Contoso West.

**Learn more:** [Plan a Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/secure-external-access-resources) · [Quickstart: Add a guest user and send an invitation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/b2b-quickstart-add-guest-users-portal)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1.  
  
You need to enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session control for Site1.  
  
Which type of policy should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies require a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy to route the applicable application traffic through Conditional Access App Control. That Conditional Access policy establishes the permissions and traffic control required for session control to operate.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad) · [Use Defender for Cloud Apps Conditional Access app control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/conditional-access-app-control-how-to-overview)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that contains a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1.  
  
You need to receive a notification when a user downloads more than 50 files from Site1 within one minute.  
  
Which policy type should you create in the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps activity policies can filter download activities and configure repeated-activity match parameters with a specified count and time frame. They can therefore generate an alert when a user exceeds 50 downloads in one minute.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create activity policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/user-activity-policies)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a separate access review for every role.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A fallback reviewer receives an access review when the user being reviewed has no manager specified in Microsoft Entra ID. Separate role-based reviews do not configure the department managers as the users' managers or otherwise change the reviewer routing, so they do not ensure that each department manager receives reviews for that department.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an access review of Azure resource and Microsoft Entra roles in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-create-roles-and-resource-roles-review) · [Create an access review of groups and applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review)

questions.question:
Solution: Modify the properties of the IT administrator user accounts.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
With **Manager** selected as the reviewer, Microsoft Entra sends the access review to each user’s configured manager. A fallback reviewer is used when no manager is specified. Setting each IT administrator’s manager property to the manager of the appropriate department causes those department managers to receive the reviews instead of the fallback reviewer.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an access review of Azure resource and Microsoft Entra roles in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-create-roles-and-resource-roles-review)

questions.question:
Solution: Set **Reviewers** to **Member (self)**.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The **Members (self)** reviewer type requires each member to review their own access. It does not assign the review to each user’s manager, so it cannot ensure that department managers receive the reviews for their departments. Microsoft Entra’s **Manager** reviewer type is the option that has managers review the access of people they manage.\
\
**Learn more:** [Plan a Microsoft Entra access reviews deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/deploy-access-reviews)

questions.question:
Solution: Add every manager as a fallback reviewer.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Fallback reviewers do not provide department-based routing. They are assigned only when the primary manager reviewer is unavailable or the reviewed user has no manager in the directory, so adding all department managers as fallback reviewers would not ensure that each department's manager receives that department’s access reviews.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an access review of groups and applications - Microsoft Entra ID Governance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant containing 1,000 users. The users have Microsoft Entra Suite licenses.  
  
You are deploying Global Secure Access.  
  
You need to ensure that connections to www.microsoft.com bypass Global Secure Access.  
  
Which profiles should you update?

options.text: Microsoft traffic profile and Internet access profile only
Microsoft traffic profile, Private access profile, and Internet access profile

questions.explanation:
FQDNs such as www.microsoft.com are governed by the Microsoft traffic profile, and the Internet Access profile does not separately acquire destinations that are already covered by the Microsoft traffic profile. Setting the applicable rule to Bypass in the Microsoft traffic profile alone is therefore sufficient to keep that traffic off the Global Secure Access tunnel; updating the Internet Access or Private Access profiles is unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft traffic profile overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/concept-microsoft-traffic-profile)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that users can access resources in the subscription only from a device with the Global Secure Access client connected.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Enable tagging to enforce tenant restrictions.

questions.explanation:
Global Secure Access signaling for Conditional Access enables the compliant-network check, which lets Microsoft Entra Conditional Access identify traffic connected through the tenant’s Global Secure Access service. After signaling is enabled, a compliant-network named location and Conditional Access policy can enforce the access requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable Compliant Network Check with Conditional Access - Global Secure Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-compliant-network)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that users can access resources in the subscription only from a device with the Global Secure Access client connected.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure Sign-in options from the Settings app.
Modify the Local intranet Zone settings.
Install the Azure AD Connect Authentication Agent.

questions.explanation:
Azure AD Seamless SSO uses Kerberos-based integrated Windows authentication. The Azure AD Seamless SSO URL must be added to users’ Local intranet zone settings so browsers send the required Kerberos tickets to the service endpoint. Microsoft documents configuring `https://autologon.microsoftazuread-sso.com` in the intranet zone through Group Policy.

**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Microsoft Entra seamless single sign-on](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sso-quick-start)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD Premium P2 tenant.  
  
You create a Log Analytics workspace.  
  
You need to make sure that Azure AD audit log information can be viewed by using Azure Monitor.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the Diagnostics settings for Azure AD.

questions.explanation:

Selecting the audit-log category and sending it to a Log Analytics workspace is required before the audit data can be queried or visualized there. You have an Azure subscription that contains a Linux virtual machine named VM1.  
  
You need to configure enhanced security for VM1. The solution must satisfy the following requirements:  
  
- Ensure users can sign in to VM1 by using their Microsoft Entra credentials.  
- Ensure users authenticate by using multi-factor out-of-band authentication.  
- Prevent users from signing in to VM1 by using passwords.  
  
Which two authentication methods can you include in the solution? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure Linux VMs uses OpenSSH certificate-based sign-in and supports Conditional Access policies that require multifactor authentication. Microsoft Authenticator and FIDO2 security keys support passwordless Microsoft Entra authentication; FIDO2 uses a security key plus user verification, and Authenticator can provide passwordless MFA through the registered mobile device.

**Learn more:** [Sign in to a Linux virtual machine in Azure by using Microsoft Entra ID and OpenSSH](https://learn.microsoft.com/sl-si/entra/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-linux) · [How to enable passkeys (FIDO2) in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-authentication-passkeys-fido2)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that includes the following objects:  
  
- A device named Device1  
- Users named User1, User2, User3, User4, and User5  
- Groups named Group1, Group2, Group3, Group4, and Group5  
  
The groups are configured as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706332344-i19ox5bk.png)  
  
To which groups can a Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E5 license be assigned directly?

options.text: Group1, Group2, Group3, Group4, and Group5
Group1, Group2, Group4, and Group5 only

questions.explanation:
Group-based licensing supports security groups and Microsoft 365 groups, including groups with assigned membership and dynamic user membership. Licenses are assigned to users, so a dynamic device group cannot receive a user license assignment. Group1, Group2, Group4, and Group5 are eligible, while Group3 is not.

**Learn more:** [What is group-based licensing? - Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/concept-group-based-licensing) · [Assign or unassign licenses to a group in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/manage-group-licenses?view=o365-worldwide)

You have an Azure subscription containing a storage account named `storage1` and a web app named `WebApp1`. `WebApp1` uses a system-assigned managed identity.  
  
You need to make sure that `WebApp1` can read and write files to `storage1` by using that system-assigned managed identity.  
  
What should you configure for `storage1` in the Azure portal?
questions.explanation:
Azure RBAC role assignments grant a managed identity permissions to access Azure Storage data. Assigning the web app’s system-assigned managed identity an appropriate Storage Data Contributor role at the storage-account scope is configured through **Access control (IAM)**.\
\
**Learn more:** [Authorize access to data in Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/authorize-data-access)

You need to deploy Global Secure Access.  
  
In which environments can the Global Secure Access client be installed?

options.text: Contractors, Developers, Frontline workers, Office staff, and Senior managers
Frontline workers and Senior managers only
Developers, Office staff, and Senior managers only

questions.explanation: Global Secure Access clients require Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid-joined Windows 10/11 devices (64-bit), support Azure Virtual Desktop single-session and Windows 365, but do not support AVD multi-session or registered devices.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant containing the groups shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783710450024-3c9ueejs.png)  
  
You need to implement Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for these groups.  
  
Which groups can be managed by using PIM?
questions.explanation:
PIM for Groups can manage cloud security groups and Microsoft 365 groups with assigned membership. Dynamic groups cannot be managed by PIM for Groups; therefore, the assigned security group and assigned Microsoft 365 group are eligible.\
\
**Learn more:** [Bring groups into Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/groups-discover-groups)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant containing the groups shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783710450024-3c9ueejs.png)  
  
You need to implement Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for these groups.  
  
Which groups can be managed by using PIM?
questions.explanation:
PIM settings for a Microsoft Entra role apply to every assignment of that role, whereas PIM for groups supports separate membership activation settings for each group. Two role-assignable security groups can therefore provide distinct workflows: one without approval for User1 and one requiring User3's approval for User2. Each group can then be assigned the User Administrator role.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra role settings in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-change-default-settings) · [Configure PIM for Groups settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/groups-role-settings)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual machine named VM1. VM1 has the following configuration:  
  
- Private IP address: 172.16.1.5  
- Public IP address: 108.143.161.25  
- System-assigned managed identity status: On  
  
You install an app named App1 on VM1.  
  
You need to configure App1 to request an app-only access token by using the managed identity.  
  
Which IP address should App1 use for the request?
questions.explanation:
Applications running on an Azure VM obtain a managed identity access token from the Azure Instance Metadata Service endpoint at `http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token`. This link-local address is reachable only from within the VM and is independent of the VM’s assigned public or private IP address.

**Learn more:** [Use managed identities on a virtual machine to acquire an access token](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-to-use-vm-token) · [Azure Instance Metadata Service for virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/instance-metadata-service)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You have 500 devices running either Windows 11, macOS, iOS, or Android that are enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You plan to deploy the Global Secure Access client.  
  
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, you download the Global Secure Access client for each operating system.  
  
You need to deploy the client to the macOS devices by using Intune.  
  
Which file extension should you use when uploading the client to Intune?
questions.explanation:
The Global Secure Access client for macOS is distributed as `GlobalSecureAccessClient.pkg`. Intune deploys this as a macOS app (PKG), so the uploaded installer must use the `.pkg` extension.\
\
**Learn more:** [Install the Global Secure Access client for macOS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-install-macos-client)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to add Facebook as a social identity provider to the tenant. What should you do first?

options.text: Set Enable guest self-service sign up via user flows to Yes.

questions.explanation:
Facebook sign-in is available through self-service sign-up user flows. The tenant must have guest self-service sign-up via user flows enabled before Facebook can be used as a social identity provider.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add Facebook as an identity provider for External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/facebook-federation) · [Add B2B Guest Sign-in](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/self-service-sign-up-user-flow)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You need to ensure that only users from specified external domains can be invited as guests to the tenant.  
  
Which settings should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings include collaboration restrictions, where an administrator can allow invitations only to specified domains. Domains outside that allowlist cannot receive B2B guest invitations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure external collaboration settings for B2B in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/uk-ua/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You need to ensure that only users from specified external domains can be invited as guests to the tenant.  
  
Which settings should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID User consent settings control whether users can grant applications permission to access organizational data. Restricting or disabling user consent causes applications that need consent to require administrator approval; an admin consent workflow can then let users submit approval requests. [Configure how users consent to applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-user-consent?tabs=azure-powershell)

**Learn more:** [Configure how users consent to applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-user-consent?tabs=azure-powershell) · [Configure the admin consent workflow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-admin-consent-workflow)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company recently deployed Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
While reviewing the roles in PIM, you find that all 15 users in the company’s IT department have permanent Security administrator rights.  
  
You need to ensure that IT department users can access the Security administrator role only when necessary.  
  
What should you configure for the Security administrator role assignment?

options.text: Expire eligible assignments after from the Role settings details
Expire active assignments after from the Role settings details

questions.explanation:
An Eligible PIM assignment requires the user to activate the Security administrator role before using its permissions, providing just-in-time access. An Active assignment grants the role’s privileges continuously; expiration settings merely limit an assignment’s overall duration and do not make access activation-based.

**Learn more:** [Assign Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-add-role-to-user)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription, a Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account, and an Amazon Web Services (AWS) account.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for assessing the risks associated with privilege assignments across all platforms. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Permissions Management provides Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM) to assess privilege assignment risks across Azure, AWS, and GCP from a unified platform, minimizing administrative overhead.

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription, a Google Cloud Platform (GCP) account, and an Amazon Web Services (AWS) account.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for assessing the risks associated with privilege assignments across all platforms. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: Assign Admin1 the Authentication Administrator role for Au1.

questions.explanation:
Security defaults cannot be enabled while any Conditional Access policy exists, including policies that are disabled or in report-only mode. CAPolicy1 must therefore be deleted before Security defaults can be enabled. Managing Security defaults also requires an appropriate tenant-level administrative role; an Authentication Administrator role scoped to an administrative unit does not provide that permission.

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1 and a Microsoft Teams team named Team1. The subscription includes five security groups named Group1, Group2, Group3, Group4, and Group5.  
  
You need to implement access packages for Site1 and Team1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Members of Group3 must be able to request access to Site1 only.  
- Members of Group1 must be able to request access to Site1 and Team1.  
- Members of Group4 must be able to request access to Site1 and Team1.  
- Only members of Group2 must be able to approve access package requests from Group1 members.  
- Only members of Groups must be able to approve access package requests from Group3 and Group4 members.  
  
What is the minimum number of access packages that you should create?
questions.explanation:
An access package can include multiple resource roles, including SharePoint sites and Teams, and it can have multiple assignment policies. A Site1-only package can serve Group3, while a second package that contains both Site1 and Team1 can serve Groups1 and 4 through separate policies. Each policy can restrict the requesting group and configure its designated approvers, so the differing approval requirements do not require additional access packages.

**Learn more:** [Create an access package in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-create) · [Change request settings for an access package in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-request-policy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure Automation account named Automation1.  
  
You need to provide Automation1 with access to Azure resources. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure that any permissions granted to Automation1 are removed when the account is deleted.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
A system-assigned managed identity is attached directly to a single Azure resource and shares that resource’s lifecycle. When the Automation account is deleted, Azure deletes the identity, eliminating its ability to authenticate and use the Azure RBAC permissions granted to it. Managed identities also remove the need to manage client-secret or certificate credentials.

**Learn more:** [Managed identities for Azure resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview) · [Managed identities glossary](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/managed-identities-glossary)

You have multiple on-premises devices running either Windows or Linux.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You configure Microsoft Entra Internet Access.  
  
You need to ensure that every on-premises device accesses the internet through Global Secure Access.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Entra admin center?

options.text: Deploy the Global Secure Access client.

questions.explanation:
A remote network connects an on-premises network to Global Secure Access through an IPsec or GRE tunnel from customer-premises equipment, enabling site-level traffic forwarding without requiring a client on each device. This supports mixed Windows and Linux device environments.

**Learn more:** [Understand remote network connectivity - Global Secure Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/concept-remote-network-connectivity) · [Quickstart: Create a remote network, apply Conditional Access, and review the logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/quickstart-remote-network)

You have a Microsoft 365 tenant. All users have computers running Windows 10. Most computers are company-owned and joined to Azure Active Directory (Azure AD). Some computers are user-owned and only registered in Azure AD.  
  
You need to prevent users who access Microsoft SharePoint Online from their user-owned computers from downloading or syncing files. Other users must **not** be restricted.  
  
Which policy type should you create?

options.text: a Microsoft Cloud App Security activity policy that has Microsoft Office 365 governance actions configured
an Azure AD conditional access policy that has session controls configured
an Azure AD conditional access policy that has client apps conditions configured
a Microsoft Cloud App Security app discovery policy that has governance actions configured

questions.explanation:
Azure AD Conditional Access session controls can use app-enforced restrictions for SharePoint Online to limit unmanaged devices to browser-only access without download or sync capability. This allows Azure AD–joined company-owned devices to retain full access while Azure AD–registered user-owned devices are restricted.

**Learn more:** [Use app-enforced restrictions - SharePoint in Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/app-enforced-restrictions) · [Build Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
You need to determine which users access Facebook from their devices and browsers. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a Defender for Cloud Apps access policy.
Create an app configuration policy in Microsoft Endpoint Manager.
From the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal, unsanction Facebook.

questions.explanation:
In Defender for Cloud Apps, marking a discovered app as **Unsanctioned** enables easier monitoring of its use through Cloud Discovery filters. Cloud Discovery associates app activity with users and devices, so this supplies the required visibility without the administrative overhead of creating a new access, Conditional Access, or device-management policy.

**Learn more:** [Govern discovered apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/governance-discovery) · [Cloud discovery policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/policies-cloud-discovery)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You create an access review named Review1. Review1 requires Microsoft 365 group owners to review guest user access to their groups every six months.  
  
You need to ensure that guest users are removed automatically if the group owners do not review Review1 membership.  
  
Which settings should you configure for Review1?
questions.explanation:
Upon completion settings contain both the action for reviewers who do not respond and automatic application of the review results. Setting nonresponses to remove access and enabling automatic application removes the affected guest users’ group access when the review period ends.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an access review of groups and applications in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You create an access review named Review1. Review1 requires Microsoft 365 group owners to review guest user access to their groups every six months.  
  
You need to ensure that guest users are removed automatically if the group owners do not review Review1 membership.  
  
Which settings should you configure for Review1?

options.text: a built-in role-based access control (RBAC) role
a custom role-based access control (RBAC) role

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Graph application permissions support app-only access, in which a service calls Microsoft Graph with its own identity and no signed-in user. They require administrator consent and are appropriate for a background service that collects sign-in audit logs.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Microsoft Graph permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/permissions-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You also have an Azure subscription linked to a Microsoft Entra tenant. The tenant contains a user named User1.  
  
You plan to deploy Microsoft Entra Permissions Management.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can onboard the Azure subscription to Permissions Management. The solution must follow the principle of least principle.  
  
Which Microsoft Entra role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Permissions Management Administrator built-in role can manage all aspects of Microsoft Entra Permissions Management, including onboarding cloud subscriptions. It provides the required service-specific administrative capability without the broad tenant-wide privileges of the Global Administrator role.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You purchase the app governance add-on license.  
  
You need to turn on app governance integration.  
  
Which portal should you use?

options.text: the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal
the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
App governance is enabled in the Microsoft Defender security experience by navigating to Settings, then Cloud Apps, then App governance, and selecting **Use app governance**. In the portal naming used here, this corresponds to Microsoft 365 Defender.\
\
**Learn more:** [Turn on app governance for Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/app-governance-get-started)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises application named App1.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You plan to publish App1 by using Microsoft Entra Private Access.  
  
You need to enable the Private access profile.  
  
Which blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Private Access traffic forwarding profile is enabled in the Microsoft Entra admin center under **Global Secure Access > Connect > Traffic forwarding**. This profile routes traffic to private resources such as App1 through Microsoft Entra Private Access.\
\
**Learn more:** [How to manage the Private Access traffic forwarding profile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-manage-private-access-profile)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises application named App1.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You plan to publish App1 by using Microsoft Entra Private Access.  
  
You need to enable the Private access profile.  
  
Which blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center should you use?

options.text: user accounts and Storage Service Encryption
user-assigned managed identities and Azure Key Vault
user accounts and Azure Key Vault
system assigned managed identities and Storage Service Encryption

questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault securely stores API secrets. A user-assigned managed identity can be associated with multiple virtual machines, allowing each App1 host to use Microsoft Entra authentication and receive the same authorized access without credentials embedded in application code. Its shared, independent lifecycle avoids managing separate identities and permissions for every VM.

**Learn more:** [Managed identities for Azure resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview) · [What is Azure Key Vault?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/basic-concepts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the Azure resources displayed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709443442-ipcvrqu7.png)  
  
To which identities can the Contributor role be assigned for RG1?
questions.explanation:
Azure RBAC roles, including Contributor at a resource-group scope, can be assigned to users, security groups, service principals, and managed identities. A dynamic-membership security group remains a valid security-group principal for Azure RBAC; a system-assigned managed identity can receive a role assignment; and an enterprise application has a service principal that can receive one.

**Learn more:** [Assign Azure roles using the Azure portal - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal) · [Understand Azure role assignments - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
Several third-party apps access resources in the subscription.  
  
You need to monitor access by the third-party apps.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
An OAuth app policy monitors third-party OAuth applications that have been granted access to Microsoft 365 data and evaluates their requested permissions. Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps uses these policies to investigate OAuth app permissions and can alert on or remediate risky apps.\
\
**Learn more:** [Control cloud apps with policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/control-cloud-apps-with-policies) · [Manage OAuth apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/manage-app-permissions)

questions.question:
You have accounts on the following cloud platforms:  
  
- Azure  
- Alibaba Cloud  
- Amazon Web Services (AWS)  
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP)  
  
You configure an Azure subscription to use Microsoft Entra Permissions Management to manage permissions in Azure only.  
  
Which other cloud platforms can Permissions Management manage?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Permissions Management supported authorization systems in Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Alibaba Cloud was not supported, so the additional manageable platforms are AWS and GCP.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Graph permissions management API overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/permissions-management-api-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant that includes a user named User1.  
  
User1 must manage license assignments and reset user passwords.  
  
Which role should be assigned to User1?
questions.explanation:
The User Administrator role can manage users, including user license assignments and password resets. The License Administrator role manages licenses but does not provide password-reset permissions, while the Helpdesk Administrator role is intended for password support rather than license management.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708910241-0zpxu7mm.png)  
  
You add an enterprise application named App1 to Azure AD and configure User1 as the owner of App1. App1 requires admin consent to access Azure AD before it can be used.  
  
You configure the Admin consent requests settings as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708914291-m8p51gr7.png)  
  
Admin1, Admin2, Admin3, and User’ are added as reviewers.  
  
Which users can review and approve the admin consent requests?
questions.explanation:
Designation as an admin-consent reviewer does not elevate a user's permissions. A reviewer must also hold a role that can grant tenant-wide admin consent in order to approve a request. Cloud Application Administrator and Application Administrator have that authority, whereas Security Administrator and an application owner with no directory role do not.

**Learn more:** [Configure the admin consent workflow - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-admin-consent-workflow) · [Review and take action on admin consent requests - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/review-admin-consent-requests)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You find that a large number of new apps have been added to the tenant.  
  
You need to establish an approval process for new enterprise applications.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal, create a Cloud Discovery anomaly detection policy.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure the Admin consent settings.
From the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal, configure an app connector.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure an access review.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Admin consent settings provide the admin consent workflow, allowing users to request approval for apps and routing those requests to designated reviewers. This centralizes approval of enterprise application consent and helps prevent unapproved apps from being added through user consent.

**Learn more:** [Configure the admin consent workflow - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-admin-consent-workflow)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a web app named App1.  
  
Guest users are routinely granted access to App1.  
  
You need to ensure that guest users who have **not** accessed App1 in the last 30 days have their access removed. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: an access review for application access

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra access review for application access can be scoped to guest users assigned to App1. Its inactivity recommendation evaluates the user's last sign-in to that application; users with no app sign-in during the previous 30 days are recommended for denial. Configuring automatic application of review results removes the denied users' App1 access with minimal ongoing administration.

**Learn more:** [Create an access review of groups and applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review) · [Manage access with access reviews](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/manage-access-review)

You work for Contoso, Ltd., which has a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com.  
  
Contoso is collaborating on a project with these two partner companies:  
  
- A. Datum Corporation, which has a Microsoft Entra tenant named adatum.com.  
- Fabrikam, Inc., which has a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com.  
  
When you try to invite a new guest user from adatum.com to contoso.com, an error message appears.  
  
You can successfully invite a new guest user from fabnkam.com to contoso.com.  
  
You need to be able to invite new guest users from adatum.com to contoso.com.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra collaboration restrictions control B2B guest invitations by external domain through an allowlist or blocklist. Permitting adatum.com in the applicable restriction allows invitations from that domain, while guest invite settings control who may send invitations rather than which partner domain may receive them.

**Learn more:** [Allow or block B2B collaboration with organizations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/entra/external-id/allow-deny-list?azure-portal=true)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named Contoso that includes a terms of use (Toll) named Terms1 and an access package. Contoso users collaborate with an external organization named Fabrikam. Fabrikam users must accept Terms1 before they can use the access package.  
  
You need to determine which users accepted or declined Terms1.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra audit logs record terms-of-use consent events, including **Accept Terms Of Use** and **Decline Terms Of Use**, allowing the accepted or declined status for Terms1 to be identified.

**Learn more:** [Set up Microsoft Entra Terms of Use with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/terms-of-use) · [Microsoft Entra audit log activity reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/reference-audit-activities)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory Premium P2 tenant.  

You create a Log Analytics workspace.  

You need to ensure that you can view Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) audit log information by using Azure Monitor.  

What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the Diagnostics settings for Azure AD.

questions.explanation: To view Azure AD audit logs in Azure Monitor via a Log Analytics workspace, you must first configure diagnostic settings in Azure Active Directory to route audit and sign-in logs to that workspace.

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com with Azure AD Identity Protection enabled.  
  
You need to implement a sign-in risk remediation policy without blocking user access.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure access reviews in Azure AD.
Configure self-service password reset (SSPR) for all users.
Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID Protection sign-in risk policies can require multifactor authentication while allowing access. Completing MFA remediates the risky sign-in, so users must be enabled and registered for MFA before that remediation control can be used.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk-based access policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-policies)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com with Azure AD Identity Protection enabled.  
  
You need to implement a sign-in risk remediation policy without blocking user access.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft Defender portal, configure Cloud discovery.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure single sign-on (SSO) for App1.
From the Microsoft Defender portal, create an OAuth app policy.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure a traffic forwarding profile.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session controls require the application to be configured for supported single sign-on, such as Microsoft Entra ID with SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect 2.0. Configuring App1 SSO in Microsoft Entra establishes the prerequisite for onboarding the app to Conditional Access App Control and applying session policies.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting access and session controls for end-users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/troubleshooting-proxy-end-users) · [Use Defender for Cloud Apps Conditional Access app control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/conditional-access-app-control-how-to-overview)

You have an Azure subscription that contains 50 virtual machines running Windows Server.  
  
You enable Microsoft Entra login for the virtual machines.  
  
Users report that they cannot sign in to the virtual machines with their Microsoft Entra credentials.  
  
You need to ensure that users can sign in to the virtual machines.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft Entra admin center, delete the device registrations of the virtual machines.
Enable SSH client support for OpenSSH.
Ensure that the virtual machines can access https://enterpriseregistration.windows.net.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure Windows virtual machines requires outbound TCP 443 access to `https://enterpriseregistration.windows.net` for device registration. Ensuring that the VMs can reach this endpoint enables the required registration flow for Microsoft Entra sign-in.

**Learn more:** [Sign in to a Windows virtual machine in Azure by using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-windows)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the custom roles listed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708906577-j8e1jz0o.png)  
  
You need to use the Azure portal to create a custom Azure subscription role named Role3. Role3 will use the baseline permissions from an existing role.  
  
Which roles can you clone to create Role3?

options.text: built-in Azure subscription roles and Role2 only
built-in Azure subscription roles and built-in Azure AD roles only
Role1, Role2, built-in Azure subscription roles, and built-in Azure AD roles

questions.explanation:
Azure portal creation of an Azure RBAC custom role allows cloning an existing built-in or custom Azure RBAC role. Therefore, Azure subscription built-in roles and the existing Azure subscription custom role Role2 can provide the baseline permissions. Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) roles, including Role1, are directory roles and are not Azure subscription RBAC roles for this operation.

**Learn more:** [Create or update Azure custom roles using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/custom-roles-portal)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that users who access the Microsoft 365 portal in Microsoft Edge, with their browser language configured as Spanish, see a Spanish sign-in form.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Entra admin center?

options.text: From Settings for the users, configure the Usage location setting.
From Global Secure Access, configure the Session management settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Company branding supports a customized sign-in experience for a specific browser language. Configure Company branding and add Spanish as a browser language so the Spanish-specific branding and sign-in-form settings apply when the browser is set to Spanish.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add company branding to your organization's sign-in page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/how-to-customize-branding)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to query risky-user activity for the tenant.  
  
For how long are the risky-user activity logs retained?
questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Entra ID Protection, the risk-detection activity records that back the risky-user investigation are retained for a fixed 90 days regardless of license tier, which is distinct from risky-user records themselves (kept until the risk is remediated) and from risky sign-ins (retained 7, 30, or 90 days depending on license). For querying risky-user activity, 90 days is the applicable window.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data retention for reports and logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/reference-reports-data-retention)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1. Site1 contains PDF files.  
  
You need to stop users from printing the files directly from Site1.  
  
Which policy type should you create in the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal?
questions.explanation:
A session policy provides real-time controls over actions performed during a cloud-app browser session. In Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, a session policy using **Block activities** can block the **Print** activity for SharePoint Online.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad) · [Commonly used information protection policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/policies-information-protection)

questions.question:
You need to synchronize the ADatum users. The solution must satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Azure Active Directory Connect wizard, select Customize synchronization options.
From the Microsoft Azure Active Directory Connect wizard, select Change user sign-in.

questions.explanation:
`Start-ADSyncSyncCycle` triggers a Microsoft Entra Connect synchronization cycle, enabling directory changes such as user updates to be synchronized. `Set-ADSyncScheduler` configures the synchronization scheduler rather than starting a cycle.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect: ADSync PowerShell Reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/reference-connect-adsync)

questions.question:
You need to synchronize the ADatum users. The solution must satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
The Reader role grants control-plane read access to all Azure resources. Virtual Machine Contributor includes virtual machine actions such as restart, and Contributor grants management access to resources in its assigned scope, enabling creation of both virtual machines and storage accounts in RG1. Assigning these roles at the subscription and RG1 scopes requires three role assignments.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles for General - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/general) · [Azure built-in roles for Compute - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/compute)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant containing the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708192385-640uj8t9.png)  
  
The tenant has the authentication methods shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708195262-13ixxkn5.png)  
  
Which users will sign in to cloud apps by matching a number displayed in the app with a number displayed on their phone?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Authenticator phone sign-in displays a number on the sign-in screen and requires the user to enter the matching number in the Authenticator app. The Authenticator method is enabled only for Group1, whose member is User1. FIDO2 uses a security key or passkey verification, while SMS sign-in requires entering a code sent by text message. [Microsoft Learn: Passwordless sign-in with Authenticator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-passwordless-phone)

**Learn more:** [Passwordless sign-in with Authenticator - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-passwordless-phone) · [Sign in with a FIDO2 security key - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-security-key-sign-in)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to create a Conditional Access policy to control administrative access to the tenant. The solution must ensure that administrators authenticate by using a phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA) method.  
  
Which three authentication methods should you include in the solution? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra identifies Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 security keys, and certificate-based authentication (when configured to satisfy MFA) as phishing-resistant authentication methods. Voice calls, SMS, and email one-time passcodes can be obtained through social engineering or phishing and therefore do not meet a phishing-resistant MFA requirement.

**Learn more:** [Require phishing-resistant multifactor authentication for Microsoft Entra administrator roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-admin-phish-resistant-mfa) · [Microsoft Entra authentication overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/overview-authentication)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant containing cloud-based enterprise apps.  
  
You need to organize related apps into categories in the My Apps portal.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
My Apps collections group related enterprise applications and display them in separate tabs, allowing categories based on roles, tasks, or projects.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create collections on the My Apps portal - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/access-panel-collections)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to make sure that users are prompted to accept a custom terms of use (ToU) agreement when they sign in to the subscription.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Terms of Use policies are applied and enforced through Conditional Access. A Conditional Access policy can require users to accept a custom terms-of-use document during the sign-in experience before they receive access.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up Microsoft Entra Terms of Use with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/terms-of-use)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned changes to the **User administrator** role.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management role settings are configured per role and control that role’s assignment and activation properties, such as approval or multifactor-authentication requirements, assignment duration, and notifications. Changes to the User administrator role’s behavior therefore require modifying its role settings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra role settings in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-change-default-settings)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783707671630-f9sgbirx.png)  
  
User1 is the owner of Group1.  
  
You create an access review with the following settings:  
  
- What to review: Teams + Groups  
- Scope: All users  
- Group: Group1  
- Reviewers: Users review their own access  
  
Which users can perform access reviews for User3?
questions.explanation:
A self-review assigns each user the review of that user’s own access. Because User3 is a member of Group1 and is included by the All users scope, User3 performs the review for User3’s access. Microsoft Entra access reviews support guest users reviewing their own group membership.

**Learn more:** [Manage user and guest user access with access reviews](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/manage-access-review) · [Review your access to groups and applications in access reviews](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/review-your-access)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant that includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709616345-02xc78yo.png)  
  
You need to compare each user's role permissions. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft 365 admin center can compare permissions for up to three administrator roles simultaneously through its **Compare roles** feature. This permits direct comparison of the User Administrator, Password Administrator, and Application Administrator roles with minimal administrative effort.

**Learn more:** [Assign admin roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/add-users/assign-admin-roles?redirectSourcePath=%252fen-us%252farticle%252fAdd-another-admin-f693489f-9f55-4bd0-a637-a81ce93de22d&view=o365-worldwide)

A contractor uses the credentials of [email protected].  
  
You need to ensure that you can grant the contractor access to App1. The contractor must be able to authenticate as [email protected].

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1 and a Microsoft Teams team named Team1. The subscription has five security groups named Group1, Group2, Group3, Group4, and Group5.  
  
You need to implement access packages for Site1 and Team1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Members of Group3 must be able to request access to Site1 only.  
- Members of Group1 must be able to request access to Site1 and Team1.  
- Members of Group4 must be able to request access to Site1 and Team1.  
- Only Group2 members must be able to approve access package requests from Group1 members.  
- Only Group5 members must be able to approve access package requests from Group3 and Group4 members.  
  
What is the minimum number of access packages that you should create?
questions.explanation:
An access package can contain multiple resources and can have multiple assignment policies, each with different requestor groups and approval settings. One Site1-only package supports Group3 with Group5 approval. A second package containing Site1 and Team1 supports separate policies for Group1 with Group2 approval and Group4 with Group5 approval.

**Learn more:** [Change request settings for an access package in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-request-policy) · [Create an access package in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-create)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to use Microsoft Entra Permissions Management to automatically monitor permissions and create and implement right-sized roles. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should be assigned to the Permissions Management service principal?
questions.explanation:
User Access Administrator can manage Azure resource access, including creating and modifying Azure RBAC role assignments. This enables automated implementation of right-sized roles while avoiding the broader resource-management privileges included in Contributor and Owner. Azure RBAC role assignment requires `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write`, a permission granted by User Access Administrator.

**Learn more:** [Assign Azure roles using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal) · [Elevate access to manage all Azure subscriptions and management groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783707496028-s1g5mpzx.jpg)  
  
The User settings for enterprise applications are configured as follows:  
  
- Users can consent to apps accessing company data on their behalf: No  
- Users can consent to apps accessing company data for the groups they own: No  
- Users can request admin consent to apps they are unable to consent to: Yes  
- Who can review admin consent requests: Admin2, User2  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783707498029-zpp3hbo0.png)  
  
User1 tries to add an app that requires consent to access company data.  
  
Which user can provide consent?
questions.explanation:
With user consent disabled, consent must be granted by an administrator with application-consent permissions. The Application Administrator role can grant administrative consent for applications. Being configured as an admin-consent reviewer does not itself elevate privileges, and the Authentication Administrator role does not provide the required application-consent permission.

**Learn more:** [Configure the admin consent workflow - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-admin-consent-workflow) · [Troubleshoot Consent Issues in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/entra/entra-id/app-integration/troubleshoot-consent-issues)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and Conditional Access policies.  
  
You need to block access to cloud apps when a user is assessed as high risk.  
  
Which policy type should you create in the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps access policies use Conditional Access app control to provide real-time control over user logins to cloud apps, including completely blocking access when the configured risk condition applies.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps access policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/access-policy-aad) · [Control cloud apps with policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/control-cloud-apps-with-policies)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1.  
  
You must ensure that users can request access to Site1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Automatically approve requests from users according to their group membership.  
- Automatically remove access after 30 days.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure Role settings in Azure AD Privileged Identity Management.
Create a Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps access policy.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra entitlement-management access package can assign access to a SharePoint site and applies assignment policies that control eligible requestors, approval requirements, and assignment expiration. A policy can target users by group membership, require no approval for those eligible users, and expire their assignments after 30 days.

**Learn more:** [Create an access package in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-create) · [Change request settings for an access package in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-request-policy)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need the ability to create a Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policy.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, select User monitoring.
From the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, select App onboarding/maintenance.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a Conditional Access policy.
From the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, create a continuous report.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy configured to use Conditional Access App Control is required for Defender for Cloud Apps session controls, because it establishes the permissions and traffic routing needed to control a user session.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Password Protection is configured as shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706347422-bdz4c0cx.png)  
  
You evaluate the following passwords:  
  
- Pr0jectlitw@re  
- T@ilw1nd  
- C0nt0s0  
  
Which passwords will be blocked?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Password Protection normalizes common character substitutions and fuzzy-matches terms from an enforced custom banned-password list within a password. `Pr0jectlitw@re` matches both `project` and `litware`, `T@ilw1nd` matches `Tailwind`, and `C0nt0s0` matches `Contoso`. Each resulting password score is below the required five points, so each password is rejected.

**Learn more:** [Password protection in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-password-ban-bad) · [Configure custom Microsoft Entra password protection lists](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/tutorial-configure-custom-password-protection)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has purchased a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
A user named User1 is assigned the Security Administrator role.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 is able to create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a Conditional Access policy and select Require app protection policy.
Create a Conditional Access policy and select Use Conditional Access App Control.
Assign the Cloud Application Administrator role to User1.
Assign the Cloud App Security Administrator role to User1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies depend on a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy configured with the **Use Conditional Access App Control** session control. That setting routes applicable cloud-app sessions through Defender for Cloud Apps, enabling its real-time session policies.

**Learn more:** [Create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
Users authorize third-party cloud apps to access their data.  
  
You need to configure an alert that triggers when an app requires high permissions and has been authorized by more than 20 users.  
  
Which policy type should you create in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps?
questions.explanation:
OAuth app policies evaluate OAuth application attributes, including requested permission level and the number of users who authorized the app, and can generate alerts when those conditions are met.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create policies to control OAuth apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/app-permission-policy) · [Investigate and remediate risky OAuth apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/investigate-risky-oauth)

questions.question:
You have two Microsoft Entra tenants named contoso.com and fabrikam.com. Contoso.com contains the identities shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713085446-056w7eio.png)  
  
You configure cross-tenant synchronization from contoso.com to fabrikam.com.  
  
Which identities will synchronize with fabrikam.com?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra cross-tenant synchronization provisions only user objects from the source tenant into the target tenant as B2B collaboration users; groups, devices, and contacts are not synchronized by this feature. Of the identities shown, only User1 therefore synchronizes to fabrikam.com.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is cross-tenant synchronization?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/multi-tenant-organizations/cross-tenant-synchronization-overview)
