You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that has been onboarded to Microsoft Entra Permissions Management.  
  
You need to identify managed identities that have assigned permissions and remove any permissions unused for 90 days. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do in the Entra Permissions Management portal?

options.text: From Microsoft Entra Insights, review Service principals with privileged role assignments.

questions.explanation:
An Autopilot rule automates least-privilege remediation, allowing unused permissions for managed identities to be removed according to a defined inactivity period. Reports, Insights, and audit queries are primarily used to view or investigate permission data rather than automatically perform the removal.

**Learn more:** [CloudKnox Permissions Management is now in Public Preview](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft-entra-blog/cloudknox-permissions-management-is-now-in-public-preview/2464391) · [Archive for Microsoft Entra releases and announcements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/whats-new-archive)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1 and a Microsoft 365 group named Group1.  
  
You need to ensure that Group1 members can access Site1 for 90 days. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra entitlement-management access packages can grant access to SharePoint Online sites and can use an assignment lifecycle configured to expire after a specified number of days, such as 90. Expiration automatically removes the assigned access, providing time-limited access with minimal ongoing administration.

**Learn more:** [What is entitlement management?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-overview) · [Create an access package in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-package-create)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure portal, you configure the **Account lockout** settings for multifactor authentication (MFA).  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
MFA account lockout settings govern lockout behavior after failed sign-in attempts, not the handling of a user-reported fraudulent MFA prompt. Microsoft Entra’s Report suspicious activity feature records such a report as high user risk; risk-based Conditional Access policies or automation are required to block access automatically.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings) · [Prevent attacks using smart lockout](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-smart-lockout)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure portal, configure the **Block/unblock users** settings for multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Blocking or unblocking users is a manual MFA administration function; it does not automatically block a user when that user reports an unsolicited MFA request. Microsoft Entra’s current suspicious-activity reporting feature records such a report as high user risk, which requires an appropriate risk-based policy or automation for automatic access blocking. The legacy Block/unblock users feature was removed on March 1, 2025.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure portal, you configure the **Notifications** settings for multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
MFA notification settings do not automatically block a user account after the user reports a fraudulent verification request. Microsoft distinguishes notification settings from the fraud-reporting capability; the current Report suspicious activity feature records such reports as high user risk, and risk-based policies or remediation workflows are required to restrict access automatically. [Configure Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings)\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure portal, you configure the Fraud alert settings for multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: Azure AD MFA fraud alert settings enable users to report fraudulent MFA requests as suspicious activity, and when configured appropriately, users can be automatically blocked for MFA until remediated.

questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure Active Directory admin center, you configure the **Block/unblock users** settings for multifactor authentication (MFA).  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Block/unblock users manages MFA-blocked accounts; it does not cause a report of an unsolicited Microsoft Authenticator request to automatically block the reporting user. That outcome requires MFA fraud-reporting functionality. Microsoft Entra’s current replacement, Report suspicious activity, lets users report fraudulent MFA requests and marks them as high user risk; subsequent automatic access restriction requires an appropriate risk-based policy or workflow.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and Yammer.  
  
You need to prevent users from signing in to Yammer from high-risk locations.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps access policies can block access to a cloud app based on conditions including location or IP address. An access policy scoped to Yammer and the applicable high-risk location condition enforces the required sign-in restriction.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create access policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/access-policy-aad)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to change the settings of the User administrator role to meet the technical requirements.  
  
Which two actions should you perform for the role? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Select Require ticket information on activation.
Modify the Expire eligible assignments after setting.

questions.explanation:
Requiring justification and approval to activate a role only has an effect on eligible assignments, since activation is an eligible-role concept; active assignments grant standing access with no activation step for a justification or approval workflow to attach to. To enforce justification and approval on activation for the User administrator role, the assignment type must first be changed to Eligible for all members, and the Require justification on activation setting must be enabled.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra role settings in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-change-default-settings)

questions.question:
You need to configure MFA settings for users who connect from the Boston office. The solution must satisfy the authentication and access requirements.  
  
What should you include in the configuration?

options.text: named locations that have a private IP address range
named locations that have a public IP address range
trusted IPs that have a public IP address range
trusted IPs that have a private IP address range

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra cloud-based MFA uses trusted IP ranges to bypass MFA prompts for users signing in from a defined corporate network. Those trusted IP ranges must be public IP address ranges, because Microsoft Entra evaluates the public internet-facing address of the office connection rather than its private internal addresses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant and a .NET web application named App1.  
  
You need to register App1 for Azure AD authentication.  
  
What should you configure for App1?
questions.explanation:
A web application registration must include a redirect URI (reply URL), which is the approved endpoint to which Microsoft Entra ID sends the authentication response. Bundle IDs and package names are mobile-platform identifiers, and an executable name is not the web-app registration setting. [Microsoft Learn: Register an application with the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth-register-app-v2)\
\
**Learn more:** [Register an application with the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth-register-app-v2)

questions.question:
You need to address the guest-user invitation issue.  
  
What should you do for the Azure AD tenant?

options.text: Configure the Continuous access evaluation settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID External collaboration settings contain Guest invite settings, including the option to limit guest invitations to users assigned specific administrator roles. This replaces the permissive setting that allows anyone in the organization, including guests and non-administrators, to invite guests.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure external collaboration settings for B2B in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned changes for Package1.  
  
Which users can create and manage the access review?
questions.explanation:
For an access package, Microsoft Entra permits Global Administrators, Identity Governance Administrators, the relevant catalog owner, and the relevant access package manager to create and manage access reviews. Of the listed roles, only the Identity Governance Administrator assignment meets that requirement; User5 has this role.\
\
**Learn more:** [Plan a Microsoft Entra access reviews deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/deploy-access-reviews) · [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned changes for Package1.  
  
Which users can create and manage the access review?

options.text: Change Membership type of IT_Group1 to Dynamic User.
Change Membership type of IT Group1 to Dynamic Device.

questions.explanation:
A group must be created as a role-assignable group before it can receive a Microsoft Entra directory role such as Device Administrators. The `isAssignableToRole` setting is available only when creating a new group and cannot be applied to an existing group. Role-assignable groups also require assigned, rather than dynamic, membership; adding an owner does not make a group eligible for role assignment.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Entra groups to manage role assignments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/groups-concept) · [Create a role-assignable group in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/groups-create-eligible)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned changes for litware.com.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Azure AD Connect cloud sync between the Azure AD tenant and litware.com
Azure AD Connect to include the litware.com domain
staging mode in Azure AD Connect for the litware.com domain

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is designed to synchronize a new, disconnected AD DS forest to the same Microsoft Entra tenant when an existing forest is already synchronized by Microsoft Entra Connect Sync. This supports the requirement to avoid establishing a trust between adatum.com and litware.com.\
\
**Learn more:** [Integrate an existing forest and a new forest with a single Microsoft Entra tenant using Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/cloud-sync/tutorial-existing-forest) · [What is Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/entra/identity/hybrid/cloud-sync/what-is-cloud-sync)

questions.question:
You need to resolve the sales department users' issue.  
  
What should you configure in the Azure AD tenant?
questions.explanation:
The **Maximum number of devices** setting in Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Device settings controls how many Microsoft Entra joined or registered devices each user can have. Setting it to 10 resolves the device-limit issue for sales users. [Manage devices in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/manage-device-identities)\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage devices in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/manage-device-identities)

questions.question:
You need to resolve the sales department users' issue.  
  
What should you configure in the Azure AD tenant?

options.text: Select Require ticket information on activation.
Modify the Expire eligible assignments after setting.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management uses eligible assignments for just-in-time role access: an eligible user must activate the role when it is needed, whereas an active assignment grants the role continuously. Setting an expiration for eligible assignments limits how long those eligible assignments can remain available; configuring it for one year meets the required maximum duration.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra role settings in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-change-default-settings) · [Assign Microsoft Entra roles in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-add-role-to-user)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that contains a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can create new catalogs and add1 resources to catalogs they own.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Roles and administrators blade, modify the Groups administrator role.
From the Roles and administrators blade, modify the Service support administrator role.
From the Identity Governance blade, modify the Entitlement management settings.
From the Identity Governance blade, modify the roles and administrators for the General catalog.

questions.explanation:
The entitlement-management **Catalog creator** role permits a user to create and manage catalogs. A user who creates a catalog becomes its first catalog owner and can add resources they own to that catalog. Catalog creators are assigned through the Entitlement management settings under Identity Governance.

**Learn more:** [Delegate access governance to catalog creators in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-delegate-catalog) · [Delegation and roles in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-delegate)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a new Microsoft 365 E5 tenant.  
  
You need to make sure that users connecting to the Microsoft 365 portal from an anonymous IP address are prompted to use multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID Protection classifies an anonymous IP address as a sign-in risk detection. A sign-in risk policy can require MFA to remediate a risky sign-in. User risk policies address account-level user risk, while MFA registration policies require authentication-method enrollment rather than MFA for a particular risky sign-in.

**Learn more:** [What are risk detections? - Microsoft Entra ID Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-risks) · [Sign-in risk-based multifactor authentication - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-risk-based-sign-in)

questions.question:
You need to satisfy the planned changes and technical requirements for App1.  
  
What should you implement?

options.text: a policy set in Microsoft Intune
an app configuration policy in Microsoft Intune
an app registration in Azure AD

questions.explanation:
An Azure AD app registration provides App1 with an application identity for Azure AD authentication and allows the required web redirect URI, `https://contoso.com/auth-response`, to be configured. Redirect URIs for web applications are configured in the app registration’s platform settings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Register an application with the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth-register-app-v2)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, you add the Microsoft Azure app connector.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Azure connector monitors Azure Resource Manager activities only. OAuth app-permission monitoring in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps applies to supported platforms such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Salesforce; adding the Azure connector does not provide that OAuth visibility.\
\
**Learn more:** [How Defender for Cloud Apps helps protect your Azure environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/protect-azure) · [Manage OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/manage-app-permissions)

questions.question:
Solution: From the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, you add the Amazon Web Services app connector.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
OAuth app monitoring in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps applies to connected Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Salesforce platforms. The Amazon Web Services connector is for AWS security auditing and activity visibility, so it does not enable monitoring of OAuth authentication requests.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/manage-app-permissions) · [Protect your Amazon Web Services environment - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/protect-aws)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, you add the Google Workspace app connector.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps can provide visibility into OAuth apps and audit OAuth authorization activity for Google Workspace when Google Workspace is connected through an app connector. The connector supplies the required connection to the supported platform.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/manage-app-permissions) · [Protect your Google Workspace environment - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/protect-google-workspace)

questions.question:
Solution: From the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, you add the GitHub app connector.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps provides OAuth app-permission visibility for supported platforms such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Salesforce. A GitHub app connector does not enable monitoring of OAuth authentication requests, so it does not meet this requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/manage-app-permissions) · [Connect apps to get visibility and control - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/enable-instant-visibility-protection-and-governance-actions-for-your-apps)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a user named User1. User1 is eligible for the Application Administrator role.  
  
User1 must configure a new connector group for an application proxy.  
  
What should you use to activate User1's role?

options.text: the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
Eligible Microsoft Entra administrative roles are activated through Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in the Microsoft Entra admin center, formerly the Azure Active Directory admin center. PIM temporarily makes the eligible Application Administrator assignment active so its permissions can be used.\
\
**Learn more:** [Activate Microsoft Entra roles in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-activate-role)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant containing a user named User1 and a Microsoft 365 group named Group1. User1 owns Group1.  
  
You need to make sure that User1 receives a notification every three months to validate Group1's guest membership.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra access reviews can review only guest members of a Microsoft 365 group, designate the group owner as the reviewer, recur quarterly, and notify reviewers when each review begins.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage guest access with access reviews](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/manage-guest-access-with-access-reviews) · [What are access reviews?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/access-reviews-overview)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant containing a user named User1 and a Microsoft 365 group named Group1. User1 owns Group1.  
  
You need to make sure that User1 receives a notification every three months to validate Group1's guest membership.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: a notification through the Microsoft Authenticator app
a verification code from the Microsoft Authenticator app

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Authenticator generates OATH verification codes locally every 30 seconds, so the phone does not need Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity. The user can enter that code during sign-in from the laptop, which has internet access through the wired network.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings) · [Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/authentication/multi-factor-authentication-faq)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to use Microsoft Entra workbooks to monitor identity activity.  
  
What should you configure for **Destination details** in Diagnostic settings?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra workbooks query identity activity data in a Log Analytics workspace. Configure the diagnostic setting to send the relevant Microsoft Entra logs to that workspace. [Microsoft Learn: How to use Microsoft Entra workbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-use-workbooks)

**Learn more:** [How to use Microsoft Entra workbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-use-workbooks) · [Integrate Microsoft Entra logs with Azure Monitor logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-integrate-activity-logs-with-azure-monitor-logs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant containing the objects shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706354439-jon8pwoc.png)  
  
Which objects can be added as members of Group3?
questions.explanation:
A mail-enabled security group can include user members regardless of whether they have a directly assigned license. Microsoft Entra does not support nesting security groups in mail-enabled security groups, and it does not support adding Microsoft 365 groups to security groups. Thus, User1 and User2 are the only eligible objects.

**Learn more:** [How to manage groups - Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/how-to-manage-groups?view=azureadps-2.0) · [Learn about group types, membership types, and access management - Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/concept-learn-about-groups?context=azure%2Factive-directory%2Fusers-groups-roles%2Fcontext%2Fugr-context)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to configure protected actions so that privileged users must use phishing-resistant multifactor authentication (MFA).  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure an authentication strength for the tenant.

questions.explanation:
Protected actions use a Conditional Access authentication context to apply policy enforcement to specific permissions. The authentication context must be created before it can be associated with a Conditional Access policy that requires the built-in phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength.

**Learn more:** [Add, test, or remove protected actions in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/protected-actions-add) · [What are protected actions in Microsoft Entra ID?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/protected-actions-overview)

questions.question:
Your company requires users to request access before they are able to access corporate applications.  
  
You register a new enterprise application named MyApp1 in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) and configure single sign-on (SSO) for MyApp1.  
  
Which settings should you configure next for MyApp1?
questions.explanation:
Self-service application access enables users to discover an enterprise application and request access to it. It can require approval before access is granted and lets administrators designate business approvers, satisfying a request-before-access requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable self-service application assignment - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/manage-self-service-access)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1.  
  
You need to receive a notification when a user downloads more than 50 files from Site1 within one minute.  
  
Which policy type should you create in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps?
questions.explanation:
An activity policy can monitor specified user activities, including downloads, and can detect an unexpectedly high rate of a particular activity. It can therefore generate a notification when downloads from Site1 exceed 50 within one minute.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create activity policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/user-activity-policies)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to set up continuous access evaluation for application sign-ins and assign that configuration to users who hold the Application Administrator role.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
A Conditional Access policy provides the session control used to customize Continuous Access Evaluation and supports assignments that target users based on directory roles, including Application Administrator.\
\
**Learn more:** [Build Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policies) · [Continuous access evaluation in Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-continuous-access-evaluation)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to set up continuous access evaluation for application sign-ins and assign that configuration to users who hold the Application Administrator role.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
A user-assigned managed identity can be attached to multiple supported Azure resources in the same region. Virtual machines and Azure App Service apps support user-assigned identities, and an Azure Storage account supports one user-assigned identity; therefore VM1, storage1, and WebApp1 can use Managed1.

**Learn more:** [Use managed identities for App Service and Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-managed-identity) · [Azure Storage Identity class](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/python/api/azure-mgmt-storage/azure.mgmt.storage.models.identity?view=azure-python)

options.text: Configure Azure Monitor to generate an alert if Emergency1 is modified or signs in.
Require Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM) activation of the Global administrator role for Emergency1.
Configure a conditional access policy to restrict sign-in locations for Emergency1 to only the corporate network.
Configure a conditional access policy to require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for Emergency1.

questions.explanation:
Emergency-access administrative accounts should remain independent of controls that can become unavailable or misconfigured during an outage. Requiring PIM activation, a corporate-network location, or MFA can prevent access in the emergency conditions the account is intended to address. Monitoring and alerting on modifications or sign-ins preserves access while detecting any use or unauthorized change.

**Learn more:** [Manage emergency access admin accounts - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant called contoso.com.  
  
All users who run applications registered in Azure AD are subject to Conditional Access policies.  
  
You need to prevent users from using legacy authentication.  
  
What should you include in the Conditional Access policies to filter out legacy-authentication attempts?

options.text: a cloud apps or actions condition

questions.explanation:
The Client apps condition distinguishes client types and can target legacy authentication clients, allowing a Conditional Access policy to block their sign-ins. Microsoft’s legacy-authentication policy guidance directs administrators to configure the Client apps condition and select the legacy client categories.

**Learn more:** [Block legacy authentication with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-block-legacy-authentication) · [Conditional Access conditions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-conditions)

You have a Microsoft 365 tenant that uses the `fabrikam.com` domain name.  
  
The External collaboration settings are configured as shown in the Collaboration exhibit. (Select the Collaboration tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783710451469-ffs074tl.png)  
  
The **Email one-time passcode for guests** setting is enabled for the tenant.  
  
A user named `[email protected]` shares a Microsoft SharePoint Online document library with the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783710455066-5q2pok0c.png)  
  
Which users will receive a passcode by email?
questions.explanation:
Email one-time passcode authentication is used when a guest redeems an invitation or accesses a shared resource and has no other applicable authentication method. A guest who has already redeemed an invitation is already past the redemption process and is not affected by enabling the setting. The guest who has never accessed tenant resources must redeem access and receives the passcode; an internal user does not use B2B guest redemption.

**Learn more:** [Email one-time passcode authentication for B2B guest users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/one-time-passcode) · [B2B Invitation Redemption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/redemption-experience)

You have an Azure subscription that contains the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709840666-ru0duei8.png)  
  
You need to implement Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
Which users can use PIM to activate their role permissions?
questions.explanation:
Privileged Identity Management cannot manage the classic subscription administrator roles Account Administrator or Service Administrator. SharePoint Administrator is a supported Microsoft 365 administrator role that can be managed as an eligible Microsoft Entra role and activated through PIM.\
\
**Learn more:** [Roles you can't manage in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-roles)

You need to implement Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
Which users can use PIM to activate their role permissions?
questions.explanation:
Email one-time passcode authentication is used for B2B guest users that cannot authenticate through Microsoft Entra ID, a Microsoft account, or another configured identity provider. With the feature enabled, the external contoso.com guest receives a passcode; the Outlook.com user can authenticate with a Microsoft account, and the fabrikam.com user is internal.

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant called contoso.com.  
  
You need to ensure that Azure AD External Identities pricing is calculated based on monthly active users (MAU).  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD External Identities billing is based on monthly active users, and the tenant must be linked to an Azure subscription for billing. Configuring a linked subscription enables the applicable MAU-based charges.\
\
**Learn more:** [Pricing structure and billing model for Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/external-identities-pricing)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy an app named App1 with the following configurations:  
  
- It will be registered in Microsoft Entra.  
- It will access the signed-in user's Microsoft Outlook calendar by using the Microsoft Graph API.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 can access Microsoft Graph.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: a custom role-based access control (RBAC) role
a built-in role-based access control (RBAC) role

questions.explanation:
Delegated permissions let an application call Microsoft Graph on behalf of the signed-in user and restrict access to resources that user can access. Accessing the signed-in user's Outlook calendar therefore requires a delegated Microsoft Graph permission, such as the appropriate Calendars delegated scope.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Microsoft Graph permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/permissions-overview) · [Authentication and authorization basics - Microsoft Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth/auth-concepts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Prevent User1 from being made an owner of newly registered apps.  
- Ensure that User1 can manage the Application Proxy settings.  
- Ensure that User1 can register apps.  
- Apply the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should be assigned to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Application Administrator role can create and manage application registrations and Application Proxy settings. Users assigned this role are not added as owners when they create new application registrations, satisfying the ownership restriction while providing the required capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [Delegate application management administrator permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can create access reviews for Microsoft Entra roles. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
Creating access reviews for Microsoft Entra roles is a Privileged Identity Management capability that requires the Privileged Role Administrator role at minimum. This grants the required permission without assigning broader administrative access.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an access review of Azure resource and Microsoft Entra roles in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-create-roles-and-resource-roles-review)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can create access reviews for Microsoft Entra roles. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Authentication Administrator role permits management of authentication methods, including resetting passwords, for non-administrative users. It provides the required authentication-management capability without the broader authority of Privileged Authentication Administrator, which can manage authentication methods for administrators, including Global Administrators.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [Assign Microsoft Entra roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/manage-roles-portal)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure SQL database named db1.  
  
You deploy an Azure App Service web app named App1 that delivers product information to users who connect to App1 anonymously.  
  
You need to grant App1 access to db1. The solution must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Credentials must be available only to App1.  
- Administrative effort must be minimized.  
  
Which type of credentials should you use?

options.text: an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) user account

questions.explanation:
A system-assigned managed identity is bound to the individual App Service app and is managed by Azure. Granting that identity access in Azure SQL Database enables passwordless authentication without storing or managing credentials in App1. Its lifecycle is tied to App1, which keeps the identity exclusive to that app and minimizes administration.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Connect to Azure databases from App Service without secrets using a managed identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/tutorial-connect-msi-azure-database) · [Authenticate Azure-hosted .NET apps to Azure resources using a system-assigned managed identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/azure/sdk/authentication/system-assigned-managed-identity)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You need to implement smart lockout with a lockout threshold of 10 unsuccessful sign-ins.  
  
What should you configure in the Azure AD admin center?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra smart lockout is configured in **Password protection**. Its settings include the lockout threshold, which specifies how many failed sign-ins are allowed before the initial lockout.\
\
**Learn more:** [Protect user accounts from attacks with Microsoft Entra smart lockout](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-smart-lockout)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a user named User1. The subscription is onboarded to Microsoft Entra Permissions Management.  
  
You need to grant User1 access to Permissions Management. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Follow the principle of least privilege.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Role/Policy Template subtab of Permissions Management, create a template.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a security group.
From the My Requests subtab of Permissions Management, create a new request.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, assign a role to User1.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra security group can be assigned the appropriate Permissions Management role, and its members inherit that access. Managing access through a group supports least privilege by allowing assignment of only the required role and reduces ongoing administrative work compared with maintaining individual role assignments. The Permissions Management Administrator role manages all aspects of the service, so directly assigning it to an individual is broader than necessary when only access is required.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [Use Microsoft Entra groups to manage role assignments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/groups-concept)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant called contoso.com.  
  
You implement entitlement management to provide users at Fabrikam, Inc. with access to resources. Fabrikam uses the fabrikam.com domain.  
  
Fabrikam users must be automatically removed from the tenant when their access is no longer needed.  
  
You need to configure these settings:  
  
- Block external user from signing in to this directory: No  
- Remove external user: Yes  
- Number of days before removing external user from this directory: 90  
  
What should you configure on the Identity Governance blade?
questions.explanation:
Entitlement management settings control the lifecycle of external users after they lose their last access-package assignment. These settings include whether to block sign-in, whether to remove the external user, and the number of days before removal from the directory.

**Learn more:** [Govern access for external users in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-external-users)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 2,500 users who have been assigned Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses. The licenses are assigned directly to individual users.  
  
From the **Groups** blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center, you assign Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E5 licenses to a group that contains all users.  
  
You need to remove the Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses from the users with the least administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Groups blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center
the Identity Governance blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center
the Licenses blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
The **Licenses** blade provides centralized, bulk management of a product license’s direct user assignments. Selecting the Office 365 Enterprise E3 license and removing its direct assignments removes E3 efficiently for the 2,500 users while their group-based E5 assignment remains in place. Group-based licensing is an alternative to direct user licensing, but group license management does not remove existing direct assignments.

**Learn more:** [Group-based licensing PowerShell examples](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-powershell-graph-examples) · [Assign or unassign licenses for users in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/assign-licenses-to-users?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with these settings:  
  
- Require users to register when they sign in: **Yes**  
- Number of methods required to reset: **1**  
  
Which authentication method is available to users?

options.text: an email to an address outside your organization

questions.explanation:
For SSPR configured to require one authentication method, the Microsoft Authenticator mobile-app option supports verification codes rather than push notifications. SSPR supports email one-time passcodes, including an alternate email address outside the organization, whereas FIDO2 security keys and Microsoft Teams chat are not valid SSPR reset methods.\
\
**Learn more:** [Self-service password reset deep dive - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-sspr-howitworks)

You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
All users have mobile phones and Windows 10 laptops.  
  
Users frequently work from remote locations without Wi-Fi access or mobile-phone connectivity. While at those remote locations, users connect their laptops to a wired network with internet access.  
  
You plan to implement multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Which MFA authentication method can users use from the remote location?

options.text: a verification code from the Microsoft Authenticator app
a notification through the Microsoft Authenticator app

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Authenticator generates OATH verification codes locally every 30 seconds, so a code remains available when the phone has no Wi-Fi or cellular signal. The user can enter that code on the laptop through its wired internet connection. SMS and push notifications require phone connectivity, while app passwords are for legacy applications that cannot use modern authentication.

**Learn more:** [Recommendation to migrate to Microsoft Authenticator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/recommendation-migrate-to-authenticator) · [Configure Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Automation account named Automation1 and an Azure key vault named Vault1. Vault1 holds a secret named Secret1.  
  
You enable a system-assigned managed identity for Automation1.  
  
You need to ensure that Automation1 can read the contents of Secret1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Prevent Automation1 from accessing other secrets stored in Vault1.  
- Follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Vault1, configure the Access control (IAM) settings.
From Automation1, configure the Identity settings.
From Automation1, configure the Run as accounts settings.
From Secret1, configure the Access control (IAM) settings.

questions.explanation:
Azure RBAC supports Key Vault data-plane role assignments at the individual secret scope. Assigning Automation1’s managed identity the **Key Vault Secrets User** role on Secret1 allows it to read that secret’s contents without granting access to the other secrets in Vault1.

**Learn more:** [Grant permission to applications to access an Azure key vault using Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-guide) · [Migrate Azure Key Vault from access policies to Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-migration)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 2,500 users assigned individual Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses.  
  
From the **Groups** blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center, you assign Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E5 licenses to a group that contains all users.  
  
You need to remove the Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses from the users with the least administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Licenses blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center
the Administrative units blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center
the Identity Governance blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center

questions.explanation:
Group-based licensing assigns E5 to every group member, but it does not automatically remove the users’ existing direct E3 assignments. The Licenses blade centrally lists direct assignments for a product and supports removing those direct user license assignments at scale. Direct licenses can be removed without affecting a user’s inherited group license.

**Learn more:** [Scenarios, limitations, and known issues for groups that manage licensing in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-group-advanced) · [Assign or unassign licenses for users in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/assign-licenses-to-users?view=o365-worldwide)

You have an Active Directory domain that is synchronized with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
The on-premises network includes a VPN server that authenticates against the on-premises Active Directory domain. The VPN server does **not** support Azure Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).  
  
You need to recommend a solution that provides Azure MFA for VPN connections.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: an Azure AD Password Protection proxy

questions.explanation:
Network Policy Server (NPS), with the Microsoft Entra MFA NPS extension, acts as a RADIUS server for the VPN server. It validates the on-premises Active Directory credentials and requests Azure MFA as the second authentication factor for the VPN connection.

**Learn more:** [Integrate your VPN infrastructure with Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication by using the Network Policy Server extension for Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-nps-extension-vpn)

You need to bulk-create 25 new user accounts by uploading a template file.  
  
Which properties are required in the template file?
questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with the following settings:  
  
- Require users to register when signing in: Yes  
- Number of methods required to reset: 1  
  
Which authentication method is valid for users?

options.text: an email to an address outside your organization

questions.explanation:
An alternate email address outside the organization can be registered and used for Azure AD self-service password reset. SSPR supports email-based verification, whereas smartcards, FIDO2 security tokens, and Microsoft Teams chat are not SSPR reset methods.

**Learn more:** [How self-service password reset works](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-sspr-howitworks) · [Prepopulate user authentication contact information for SSPR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/entra/identity/authentication/howto-sspr-authenticationdata)

questions.question:
You intend to deploy a new Azure AD tenant.  
  
Which multifactor authentication (MFA) method is enabled by default for the tenant?
questions.explanation:
Security defaults in a new Microsoft Entra ID tenant require users to register for and use MFA through Microsoft Authenticator notifications. SMS and voice calls are separately configurable methods, while email OTP is not the default MFA method. [Configure Security Defaults for Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/security-defaults)\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Security Defaults for Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/security-defaults) · [Microsoft Entra licensing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/licensing)

You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with these settings:  
  
- Require users to register when they sign in: Yes  
- Number of methods required to reset: 1  
  
Which authentication method is valid for users?
questions.explanation:

You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with these settings:

- Number of methods required to reset: 1  
  
Which authentication method is valid for users?

options.text: the Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool

questions.explanation:
The Conditional Access What If tool simulates a sign-in for a specific user using defined sign-in conditions, including location/IP address, and generates a report identifying the Conditional Access policies that apply or do not apply. It evaluates both enabled and report-only policies.

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You create an enterprise application collection named **HR Apps** with these settings:  
  
- Applications: App1, App2, App3  
- Owners: Admin1  
- Users and groups: HRUsers  
  
All three apps have the following **Properties** settings:  
  
- Enabled for users to sign in: Yes  
- User assignment required: Yes  
  
Visible to users: Yes -  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706515745-yvlrvbei.png)  
  
Users report that, when they open the My Apps portal, they see only App1 and App2.  
  
You need to ensure that users can see App3 as well.  
  
What should you do from App3?

options.text: From Users and groups, add HRUsers.
From Single sign-on, configure a sign-on method.
From Properties, change User assignment required to No.
From Permissions, review the User consent permissions.

questions.explanation:
A My Apps collection only displays applications to which users already have access; collection membership does not assign users to its individual applications. Since App3 requires user assignment, HRUsers must be assigned to App3 under **Users and groups**. Assigned users can then see the visible application in My Apps.

**Learn more:** [My Apps portal overview - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/myapps-overview) · [Manage users and groups assignment to an application - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/assign-user-or-group-access-portal)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713410738-es7vafh0.png)  
  
You need to grant permissions to the resources by using attribute-based access control (ABAC).  
  
To which resource can you grant permissions?
questions.explanation:
Azure ABAC adds conditions to Azure RBAC role assignments for supported Azure Storage data actions, including Blob Storage, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, and Azure Queues. A storage account is therefore the applicable resource type.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure attribute-based access control (Azure ABAC)?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/conditions-overview) · [Authorize access to Azure Blob Storage using Azure role assignment conditions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-auth-abac)

questions.question:
A user named User1 gets an error message when trying to access the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal.  
  
You need to determine the cause of the error while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra sign-in logs capture user authentication attempts and their failure details, enabling investigation of why User1 could not access the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal without first configuring log export or querying a separate analytics workspace.\
\
**Learn more:** [How to use Microsoft Entra Sign-in diagnostics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-use-sign-in-diagnostics) · [Learn about the sign-in log activity details](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-sign-in-log-activity-details)

questions.question:
A user named User1 gets an error message when trying to access the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal.  
  
You need to determine the cause of the error while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Configure password protection for the Azure AD tenant.
Configure a multi-factor authentication (MFA) registration policy.

questions.explanation:
Security defaults and Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies cannot be enabled at the same time. To use Conditional Access for customized control of access to Microsoft 365 resources, Security defaults must first be disabled.

**Learn more:** [Set up multifactor authentication for users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/security-and-compliance/set-up-multi-factor-authentication?view=o365-worldwide) · [Configure Security Defaults for Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/security-defaults)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that includes a resource group named RG1. RG1 includes an Azure Cosmos DB database named DB1 and an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster named AKS1. AKS1 uses a managed identity.  
  
You need to ensure that AKS1 can access DB1. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Ensure AKS1 uses the managed identity to access DB1.  
- Follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should be assigned to the managed identity of AKS1?

options.text: For Sub1, assign the Owner role.
For DB1, assign the Azure Cosmos DB Account Reader Role role.
For RG1, assign the Azure Cosmos DB Data Reader Role role.
For RG1, assign the Reader role.

questions.explanation:
Reading data stored in Azure Cosmos DB through a Microsoft Entra managed identity requires a Cosmos DB data-plane role, such as the Data Reader role; control-plane roles like the Cosmos DB Account Reader Role or the generic Reader role only expose account metadata and keys and cannot authorize data operations. Assigning the Data Reader role scoped to the resource group containing DB1 grants AKS1 the read access it needs while keeping the assignment as narrow as possible.

**Learn more:** [Role-based access control in Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/role-based-access-control)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
All users have mobile phones and Windows 11 laptops.  
  
Users often work from remote locations that have neither Wi-Fi access nor mobile-phone connectivity. While at these remote locations, the users connect their laptops to a wired network with internet access.  
  
You plan to implement multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Which MFA authentication method can the users use from the remote location?
questions.explanation:
Windows Hello for Business combines a device-bound credential with a PIN or biometric gesture, providing the required multiple factors and satisfying Microsoft Entra MFA requirements. It can be used on the Windows 11 laptop while the laptop accesses Microsoft 365 through the wired internet connection; it does not require Wi-Fi or mobile-phone service. App passwords bypass MFA for legacy applications, while voice verification requires phone connectivity.

**Learn more:** [How Windows Hello for Business works](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/how-it-works) · [Configure app passwords for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-app-passwords)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant called contoso.com that includes an Azure AD enterprise application named App1.  
  
A contractor uses the credentials of [email protected].  
  
You need to ensure that you can grant the contractor access to App1. The contractor must be able to authenticate as [email protected].  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a guest user account in contoso.com.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra B2B guest account lets an external contractor access resources in the contoso.com tenant while authenticating with the contractor’s existing external identity. The guest can then be assigned to the enterprise application.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add and manage B2B collaboration users in the Microsoft Entra admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/add-users-administrator)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
You need to identify the users who are eligible for the Cloud Application Administrator role.  
  
Which blade in the Privileged Identity Management settings should you use?
questions.explanation:
Cloud Application Administrator is a Microsoft Entra built-in directory role. Privileged Identity Management manages eligibility for directory roles in the Azure AD roles blade; Azure resources is used for Azure RBAC resource roles.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [Assign Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-add-role-to-user)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
You need to identify the users who are eligible for the Cloud Application Administrator role.  
  
Which blade in the Privileged Identity Management settings should you use?

options.text: From the Microsoft Defender portal, configure an app connector.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure an access review.
From the Microsoft Defender portal, create an app detection policy.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure the Admin consent settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Admin consent settings provide the admin consent workflow, allowing users to request consent for applications and designated reviewers or administrators to review and approve or deny those requests. This controls approval of new enterprise applications.

**Learn more:** [Configure the admin consent workflow - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-admin-consent-workflow)

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra applies a separate, mandatory two-gate SSPR policy to User Administrator and Password Administrator accounts; that policy prohibits security questions. Which risk detection type is categorized as a user risk?

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant called contoso.com.  
  
You plan to bulk-invite Azure AD business-to-business (B2B) collaboration users.  
  
Which two parameters are required when creating the bulk invitation? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Bulk B2B invitation CSV files require the invitee’s email address and a redirection URL. The email address identifies the external guest who receives the invitation, and the redirection URL specifies where that user is sent after accepting it. A username, shared key, and password are not required for this invitation process.\
\
**Learn more:** [Bulk invite B2B users - Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/tutorial-bulk-invite)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You configure **User consent settings** to allow users to grant consent to apps from verified publishers.  
  
You need to ensure that users can grant consent only to apps requiring low-impact permissions.

You have a Microsoft 365 tenant. The Sign-ins activity report indicates that an external contractor signed in to the Exchange admin center.  
  
You need to review access to the Exchange admin center at the end of every month and block sign-ins when necessary.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: an access package that targets users outside your directory
an access package that targets users in your directory
a group-based access review that targets guest users
an application-based access review that targets guest users

questions.explanation:
Access to the Exchange admin center is typically granted through membership in a role-assignable security group, so a group-based access review is the mechanism that lets you periodically re-certify the external contractor's continued need for that access. Scoping the review to guest users and configuring the denied-user action to block sign-in satisfies both the monthly review and the sign-in-blocking requirement.

**Learn more:** [Create an access review of groups and applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an on-premises Active Directory domain that synchronizes with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant. The tenant includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706506959-fdgt9654.png)  
  
All users work remotely. Azure AD Connect is configured in Azure AD as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706509340-3kvqrhea.png)  
  
Internet connectivity from the on-premises domain is lost. Which users can sign in to Azure AD?
questions.explanation:
Pass-through Authentication validates credentials against on-premises Active Directory through authentication agents, so a synchronized user cannot be authenticated when the on-premises environment has lost Internet connectivity to Microsoft Entra ID. Pass-through Authentication does not apply to cloud-only users, and a guest user is not authenticated through this tenant's synchronized on-premises directory. Therefore, User1 and User3 can sign in.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication: Technical deep dive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-pta-how-it-works) · [User sign-in with Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-pta)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that includes a terms of use (ToU) named Terms1.  
  
You create a Conditional Access policy named Policy1 to deploy Terms1.  
  
You need to configure Policy1 to require users to accept Terms1.  
  
Which settings should you configure for Policy1?
questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra Terms of Use policy is enforced through a Conditional Access **Grant** control. Configure Grant access and select the required Terms of Use policy so acceptance is required before access is granted.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up Microsoft Entra terms of use with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/terms-of-use) · [Conditional Access: Grant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-grant)

You create a Conditional Access policy named Policy1 to deploy Terms1.  
  
You need to configure Policy1 to require users to accept Terms1.  
  
Which settings should you configure for Policy1?

options.text: Add a custom domain name to contoso.com.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
For the tenant, **Users can register applications** is set to **No**.  
  
A user named Admin1 must deploy a new cloud app called App1.  
  
You need to ensure that Admin1 can register App1 in Azure AD. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to Admin1?

options.text: Cloud application administrator in Azure AD.
App Configuration Data Owner for Subscription1.

questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Entra ID Application Developer role grants selected users the ability to create and update application registrations when the **Users can register applications** setting is disabled. It provides the required registration permission without the broader enterprise-application management permissions of Cloud Application Administrator.

**Learn more:** [Delegate application management administrator permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra ID P2 tenant named contoso.com that includes a registered application named App1.  
  
App1 was deleted on January 1.  
  
You need to restore App1.  
  
What is the latest date on which App1 can be restored?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra application registrations remain soft-deleted and restorable for 30 days after deletion. An application deleted on January 1 can therefore be restored through January 30; after the 30-day period, it cannot be restored.\
\
**Learn more:** [Restore or remove a recently deleted application with the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-restore-app)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have three Azure subscriptions connected to one Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to assess and remediate risks related to highly privileged accounts. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) manages and monitors privileged access to Azure and Microsoft Entra resources. It helps identify unnecessary or excessive privileged assignments and remediate risk through access reviews and eligible, time-bound, just-in-time role activation, reducing standing administrative privileges.

**Learn more:** [What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-configure) · [Secure your Microsoft Entra identity infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/steps-secure-identity)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant containing the following objects:  
  
- A device named Device1  
- Users named User1, User2, User3, User4, and User5  
- Five groups named Group1, Group2, Group3, Group4, and Group5  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706501620-bc00rccf.png)  
  
The groups are configured as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706503799-8uyebkzn.png)  
  
How many licenses are consumed if you assign the Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5 license to Group1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra group-based licensing does not support nested groups. A license assigned to Group1 applies only to its immediate user members, User1 and User3; it does not flow through Group2 or Group4 to their members. Thus, two licenses are used.

**Learn more:** [Assign or unassign licenses to a group in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/manage-group-licenses?view=o365-worldwide)

options.text: Add a custom domain name to contoso.com.
Create a guest user account in contoso.com.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration lets an external person use their existing credentials while being represented by a Guest user object in the resource tenant. Creating and inviting a guest user for [email protected] enables the user to be assigned access to App1 without creating a contoso.com identity or configuring a separate federation provider.

**Learn more:** [Add and manage B2B collaboration users in the Microsoft Entra admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/add-users-administrator) · [Understand and manage the properties of B2B guest users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/user-properties)

Solution: You modify the **Diagnostics settings** from Azure AD.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Diagnostic settings control the destinations for Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) activity logs. Azure Monitor action groups define alert notification recipients, including email addresses. Changing diagnostic settings therefore does not redirect existing failed-sign-in alert emails to a new security administrator.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.question:
Solution: From Azure AD, you create an assignment for the Insights administrator role.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Insights administrator role grants access to Azure AD monitoring information; it does not alter Azure Monitor alert notification recipients. Azure Monitor action groups define who receives email notifications, so assigning this role does not redirect the existing alerts to the new security administrator.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.question:
Solution: In Azure Monitor, you modify the action group.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor action groups define the notification preferences and recipients used when an alert fires. Updating the action group’s email notification recipient directs the existing failed sign-in alerts to the new security administrator.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a data collection rule from Azure Monitor.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor data collection rules specify how telemetry is collected, processed, and sent to monitoring-data destinations. Alert notification recipients are configured through action groups, which define who receives email and other notifications when an alert fires.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data collection rules in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/data-collection/data-collection-rule-overview) · [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.question:

Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Global Administrators have administrative access to Global Secure Access, which includes Microsoft Entra Internet Access. The Global Secure Access Administrator role can create and manage all aspects of Microsoft Entra Internet Access. The Privileged Role Administrator role manages role assignments and Privileged Identity Management, rather than Microsoft Entra Internet Access configuration.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Global Secure Access built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/reference-role-based-permissions) · [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
All users have mobile phones and laptops. The users often work from remote locations that have neither Wi-Fi nor mobile phone connectivity. While at these remote locations, users connect their laptops to a wired network with internet access.  
  
You plan to implement multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Which MFA authentication method can users use from the remote location?

options.text: a verification code from the Microsoft Authenticator app

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Authenticator can generate an OATH verification code locally every 30 seconds, so entering that code on the internet-connected laptop does not require Wi-Fi or cellular service on the phone. SMS and voice MFA require phone connectivity, while security questions are not an MFA method.
