You have an Azure subscription that includes the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706514846-3xfm6oc4.png)  
  
For which resources can an access review be created?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra access reviews support group membership and enterprise application access. Privileged Identity Management also supports access reviews for Azure resource roles and Microsoft Entra directory roles. Consequently, the assigned-membership group, enterprise application, subscription-level Contributor role, and Microsoft Entra role can all be reviewed.

**Learn more:** [Plan a Microsoft Entra access reviews deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/deploy-access-reviews) · [Create an access review of Azure resource and Microsoft Entra roles in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-create-roles-and-resource-roles-review)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You must ensure that users can grant enterprise applications access to their profile. The solution must ensure users can consent only to the **User.Read** and **profile** delegated permissions.  
  
What should you configure first?
questions.explanation:
Permission classifications identify which delegated permissions are low impact and can be used by a user-consent policy. Classify **User.Read** and **profile** first; the user-consent setting can then permit consent only for the selected low-impact permissions.

**Learn more:** [Configure permission classifications - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-permission-classifications) · [Configure how users consent to applications - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-user-consent)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that uses conditional access policies.  
  
You plan to use a third-party security information and event management (SIEM) solution to analyze conditional access usage.  
  
You need to download the Azure AD log by using the administrative portal. The log file must include changes to conditional access policies.  
  
What should you export from Azure AD?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra audit logs record changes to Conditional Access policies, including policy creation, updates, and deletion. The administrative portal supports exporting activity logs in JSON, which preserves structured event data for SIEM analysis.

**Learn more:** [Conditional Access and Microsoft Entra activity logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/how-to-view-applied-conditional-access-policies) · [How to download logs in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-download-logs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a user named User1.  
  
The App registration settings for the Azure AD tenant are configured as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709836713-0537a2yf.png)  
  
User1 develops an ASP.NET web app named App1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can register App1. The solution must use the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
When the tenant setting that permits users to register applications is set to **No**, the Microsoft Entra Application Developer role allows a user to create application registrations. It grants only the required app-registration capability, whereas Application Administrator and Cloud Application Administrator grant broader application-management permissions.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles — Application Developer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#application-developer) · [Delegate application management administrator permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 2,500 users assigned Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses. The licenses are assigned individually to users.  
  
From the **Groups** blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center, you assign Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5 licenses to the users.  
  
You need to remove the Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses from the users with the least amount of administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Identity Governance blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center
the Licenses blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
The Licenses blade supports viewing the users assigned a particular product license and unassigning that license in bulk. This removes the direct Office 365 Enterprise E3 assignments while the group-based Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5 assignments remain in place.

**Learn more:** [Assign or unassign licenses to a group in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/manage-group-licenses?view=o365-worldwide) · [Assign Microsoft 365 licenses to user accounts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/assign-licenses-to-user-accounts?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You create an access review named Review1. Review1 requires Microsoft 365 group owners to review guest-user access to their groups every six months.  
  
You need to ensure that guest users are automatically removed if the group owners do not review Review1 membership.  
  
Which settings should you configure for Review1?
questions.explanation:
The **When completed** settings control the outcome after an access review ends. Configure **If reviewers don't respond** as **Remove access** and enable **Auto apply results to resource** so unreviewed guest users are automatically removed from the reviewed groups. The recurrence is configured separately under scheduling.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an access review of groups and applications - Microsoft Entra ID Governance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review)

questions.question:
You have a tenant in Microsoft Entra.  
  
You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with these settings:  
  
- Require users to register when signing in: Yes  
- Number of methods required to reset: 1  
  
Which authentication method is valid for users?

options.text: an email to an address outside your organization

questions.explanation:
For SSPR configurations requiring one authentication method, a mobile app supports verification-code validation only; mobile app notifications require two methods. Email is a supported SSPR authentication method, and users can use an email address outside the organization as their reset email address.\
\
**Learn more:** [How it works: Microsoft Entra self-service password reset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-sspr-howitworks)

questions.question:
You have a tenant in Microsoft Entra.  
  
You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with these settings:  
  
- Require users to register when signing in: Yes  
- Number of methods required to reset: 1  
  
Which authentication method is valid for users?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra application registrations support users and service principals as application owners. User1 is a user and SP1 is a service principal, whereas Group1 and Group2 are groups and cannot be assigned as owners of the application object.

**Learn more:** [application resource type - Microsoft Graph v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/application?view=graph-rest-1.0) · [Add an owner to an application using Microsoft Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/entra/entra-id/users-groups-entra-apis/add-owner-for-application-microsoft-graph)

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to prevent users from consenting to high-privilege permission requests for enterprise applications, while still allowing them to consent to low-risk permission requests.  
  
What should you modify first?
questions.explanation:
Permission classifications identify permissions by their organizational risk impact and are used by consent policies to determine the permissions to which users may consent. Classifying the permitted delegated permissions as low impact is required before applying a user-consent policy that allows only low-risk permissions; higher-privilege permissions remain outside that allowed set.

**Learn more:** [Configure permission classifications - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-permission-classifications) · [Configure how users consent to applications - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-user-consent?tabs=azure-powershell)

You plan to enhance app security for the subscription.  
  
You need to identify apps that **do not** require user authentication.

options.text: Create an OAuth policy and review alerts.

questions.explanation:

You need to identify apps that **do not** require user authentication.

options.text: the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal
the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
Eligible Microsoft Entra administrative roles are activated in Privileged Identity Management through the Azure Active Directory admin center (now named the Microsoft Entra admin center). The Application Administrator role provides the required permissions to configure Application Proxy settings, including connector groups.

questions.question:
You have Linux devices hosted on-premises.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You plan to configure Global Secure Access Internet Access.  
  
You need to make sure that the devices can connect to Global Secure Access.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Install the Azure Connected Machine agent on the devices.

questions.explanation:
Global Secure Access remote network connectivity supports Internet Access for on-premises devices such as Linux systems without installing a per-device client. A remote network establishes site-level connectivity from on-premises equipment to Global Secure Access through an IPsec tunnel.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand remote network connectivity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/concept-remote-network-connectivity)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.

You configure Microsoft Entra Internet Access for the tenant.  
  
On which devices can Global Secure Access be used?
questions.explanation:
For Windows devices, Microsoft Entra registered devices support only Private Access traffic; they do not support the Internet traffic profile used by Microsoft Entra Internet Access. A Microsoft Entra joined Windows 10 device supports the Global Secure Access client and Internet Access traffic. Therefore, only Device3 qualifies.

**Learn more:** [Install the Global Secure Access client for Microsoft Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-install-windows-client) · [Bring Your Own Device (Preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/concept-bring-your-own-device)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant called contoso.com that includes an Azure AD enterprise application named App1.  
  
A contractor uses the credentials of [email protected].  
  
You need to ensure that you can grant the contractor access to App1. The contractor must be able to authenticate as [email protected].  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
An Azure AD B2B invitation creates an external user as a guest in the tenant, allowing that user to redeem the invitation and access assigned applications by using their existing email identity. The `New-AzureADMSInvitation` cmdlet creates this guest invitation. Microsoft’s current equivalent is an Entra/Graph invitation cmdlet, but the listed Azure AD cmdlet is the applicable choice. [Microsoft Learn: Add a guest user and send an invitation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/b2b-quickstart-add-guest-users-portal)

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Learn: Add a guest user and send an invitation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/b2b-quickstart-add-guest-users-portal) · [Microsoft Learn: Manage guest accounts using Microsoft Entra PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/entra-powershell/manage-guest-users?view=entra-powershell)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 2,500 users assigned Microsoft 365 E3 licenses. The licenses are assigned directly to individual users.  
  
You assign Microsoft 365 E5 licenses to a group that contains all users.  
  
You need to remove the Microsoft 365 E3 licenses from the users while using the least administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Licenses blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center

questions.explanation:
Group-based E5 licensing supplies the replacement entitlement to all members, so the redundant direct E3 assignments can be removed in bulk. The Licenses blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center is the administrative interface for managing those direct license assignments at scale, avoiding an individual-user PowerShell operation.

**Learn more:** [PowerShell examples for group-based licensing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-powershell-graph-examples) · [Users, groups, licensing, and roles in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/directory-overview-user-model)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You create an enterprise application collection named **HR Apps** with the following settings:  
  
- Applications: App1, App2, App3  
- Owners: Admin1  
- Users and groups: HRUsers  
  
All three apps have these **Properties** settings:  
  
- Enabled for users to sign in: Yes  
- User assignment required: Yes  
- Visible to users: Yes  
  
Users report that they can see only App1 and App2 in the My Apps portal.  
  
You need to ensure that users can also see App3.  
  
What should you do from App3?

options.text: From Single sign-on, configure a sign-on method.
From Permissions, review the User consent permissions.
From Users and groups, add HRUsers.
From Properties, change User assignment required to No.

questions.explanation:
A My Apps collection displays only applications that users are already assigned to. When user assignment is required, HRUsers must be assigned directly to App3 through its Users and groups settings. Assigning the group to the collection alone does not grant access to the application.

**Learn more:** [Create collections on the My Apps portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/access-panel-collections) · [Manage users and groups assignment to an application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/assign-user-or-group-access-portal)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com with Azure AD Identity Protection policies enforced.  
  
You create an Azure Sentinel instance and configure the Azure Active Directory connector.  
  
You need to ensure that Azure Sentinel can generate incidents from risk alerts raised by Azure AD Identity Protection.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Add a Microsoft Sentinel data connector.
Configure the Notify settings in Azure AD Identity Protection.
Modify the Diagnostics settings in Azure AD.

questions.explanation:
Azure AD diagnostic settings must send the Identity Protection risk logs to the Log Analytics workspace used by Microsoft Sentinel. Those logs supply the risk-detection data that Sentinel analytics can use to create alerts and incidents; notification settings and playbooks do not ingest that data.

**Learn more:** [Integrate Microsoft Entra logs with Azure Monitor logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-integrate-activity-logs-with-azure-monitor-logs) · [Configure Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings for activity logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-configure-diagnostic-settings)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
All users have mobile phones and Windows 10 laptops.  
  
Users frequently work from remote locations without Wi-Fi access or mobile-phone connectivity. While at those remote locations, users connect their laptops to a wired network with internet access.  
  
You plan to implement multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Which MFA authentication method can users use from the remote location?

options.text: a notification through the Microsoft Authenticator app

questions.explanation:
Windows Hello for Business uses a device-bound key together with a PIN or biometric gesture, satisfying Microsoft Entra MFA requirements. The Windows laptop can communicate with Microsoft Entra through the wired internet connection, without requiring connectivity on the mobile phone. App passwords are a legacy-client workaround without an additional verification prompt, and security questions are limited to self-service password reset.

**Learn more:** [How Windows Hello for Business works](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/how-it-works) · [Configure app passwords for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-app-passwords)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant that includes a user named Admin1.  
  
You must ensure that Admin1 can perform only these tasks:  
  
- From the Microsoft 365 admin center, create and manage service requests.  
- From the Microsoft 365 admin center, read and configure service health.  
- From the Azure portal, create and manage support tickets.  
  
The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an administrative unit and add Admin1.
Enable Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for Admin1.
Assign Admin1 the Helpdesk Administrator role.
Create a custom role and assign the role to Admin1.

questions.explanation:
The Helpdesk Administrator built-in role includes permissions to create and manage Microsoft 365 service requests, read and configure Service Health in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and create and manage Azure support tickets. Assigning the built-in role avoids the administrative overhead of creating and maintaining a custom role.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [About administrator roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/add-users/about-admin-roles?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.question:
You need to address the issue affecting the sales department users.  
  
What should you configure in the Azure AD tenant?
questions.explanation:
This item comes from a case study describing sales-department users who each have up to five devices and must repeatedly contact support to join additional devices to Microsoft Entra ID. That symptom is resolved by the tenant-wide device join/quota configuration found under Device settings, not by user settings, access reviews, or security defaults.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage device identities - Configure device settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/manage-device-identities#configure-device-settings)

You have 2,500 users assigned Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses. The licenses are assigned directly to individual users.  
  
From the **Groups** blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center, you assign Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E5 licenses to a group that contains all users.  
  
You need to remove the Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses from the users with the least administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Identity Governance blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center
the Administrative units blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center

questions.explanation:
Group-based licensing is an alternative to direct user licensing; assigning E5 to the group does not remove the users’ directly assigned E3 licenses. `Set-MgUserLicense` can remove licenses from a user and can be used in a bulk PowerShell process to remove the direct E3 assignment for all affected users.

**Learn more:** [Set-MgUserLicense (Microsoft.Graph.Users.Actions)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.graph.users.actions/set-mguserlicense?view=graph-powershell-1.0) · [PowerShell examples for group-based licensing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-powershell-graph-examples)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
The Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant synchronizes with an on-premises Active Directory domain.  
  
Users access the internet through a hardware firewall at your company. Users authenticate to the firewall by using their Active Directory credentials.  
  
You plan to manage access to external applications by using Azure AD.  
  
You need to use the firewall logs to create a list of unmanaged external applications and the users who access them.  
  
What should you use to collect the information?

options.text: Cloud App Discovery in Microsoft Cloud App Security

questions.explanation:
Cloud App Discovery in Microsoft Cloud App Security analyzes firewall and proxy traffic logs to discover cloud applications in use, including shadow IT, and reports the associated users. This directly supports identifying unmanaged external applications and the users accessing them.

**Learn more:** [Cloud app discovery overview — Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/set-up-cloud-discovery) · [Create snapshot cloud discovery reports — Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/create-snapshot-cloud-discovery-reports)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
All users have mobile phones and laptops. The users often work from remote locations with no Wi-Fi access or mobile phone connectivity. At those remote locations, users connect their laptops to a wired network that has internet access.  
  
You plan to implement multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Which MFA authentication method can users use from the remote location?

options.text: a notification through the Microsoft Authenticator app

questions.explanation:
Windows Hello for Business is a device-bound, two-factor authentication method that combines the user’s laptop-held credential with a PIN or biometric gesture. It meets Microsoft Entra MFA requirements and can authenticate using the laptop’s wired internet connection, without requiring Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity on the user’s phone.

**Learn more:** [Windows Hello for Business authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-windows-hello) · [How Windows Hello for Business works](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/how-it-works)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You plan to implement Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
Which roles can you manage by using PIM?

options.text: Global Administrator and Security Administrator only
Global Administrator, Security Administrator, and Security Contributor only
Account Administrator, Global Administrator, Security Administrator, and Security Contributor only

questions.explanation:
Privileged Identity Management supports just-in-time management of Microsoft Entra roles, including Global Administrator and Security Administrator, and Azure RBAC resource roles, including Security Contributor. Account Administrator is a classic subscription administrator role that PIM cannot manage.

**Learn more:** [Roles you can't manage in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-roles) · [Assign Azure resource roles in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-resource-roles-assign-roles)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
An on-premises Active Directory domain is configured to synchronize with the Azure AD tenant. The domain contains the servers shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709829920-3ygwgax1.png)  
  
The domain controllers cannot communicate with the internet.  
  
You implement Azure AD Password Protection on Server1 and Server2.  
  
You deploy a new server named Server4 running Windows Server 2022.  
  
You need to ensure that Azure AD Password Protection continues to function if one server fails.  
  
What should you implement on Server4?

options.text: the Azure AD Password Protection proxy service

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Password Protection uses proxy servers to obtain policy data from the cloud for on-premises domain controllers. Microsoft recommends at least two Password Protection proxy servers per forest for redundancy; a second proxy lets DC agents use another available proxy if one fails.

**Learn more:** [Deploy on-premises Microsoft Entra Password Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-ban-bad-on-premises-deploy)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an Active Directory forest named contoso.com that is connected to an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com by using Azure AD Connect.  
  
You need to prevent synchronization of users whose extensionAttribute15 attribute is set to NoSync.  
  
What should you do in Azure AD Connect?

options.text: Create an inbound synchronization rule for the Windows Azure Active Directory connector.
Configure a Full Import run profile.
Create an inbound synchronization rule for the Active Directory Domain Services connector.

questions.explanation:
Attribute-based negative filtering for on-premises users is configured with an inbound synchronization rule for the Active Directory Domain Services connector. The rule is scoped to `extensionAttribute15 = NoSync` and flows `cloudFiltered = True`, which prevents the matching users from synchronizing to Microsoft Entra ID.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: Configure filtering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sync-configure-filtering)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that uses Azure AD Identity Protection and contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708205833-rrpzcz7a.jpg)  
  
Azure Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is enabled for all users.  
  
User1 triggers a medium-severity alert that requires further investigation.  
  
You need to require User1 to reset his password at the next sign-in. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Reconfigure the user risk, policy to trigger on medium or low severity.
Reset the Azure MIFA registration for User1.

questions.explanation:
Confirming a user as compromised raises the user-risk state through the administrator-confirmed compromised-user detection. The existing user risk policy, which requires high-risk users to reset their password at the next sign-in, then applies to User1 without changing the policy for other users. Microsoft Entra ID Protection documents that the admin-confirmed compromised-user detection is generated when an administrator confirms a user as compromised.

**Learn more:** [What are risk detections? - Microsoft Entra ID Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-risks) · [Risk-based access policies - Microsoft Entra ID Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 2,500 users who have been assigned Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses. The licenses are assigned directly to individual users.  
  
From the **Groups** blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center, you assign Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E5 licenses to a group that contains all users.  
  
You need to remove the Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses from the users with the least administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Licenses blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center
the Identity Governance blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center

questions.explanation:
Directly assigned licenses can coexist with licenses inherited through group membership, so assigning Office 365 Enterprise E5 to the group does not remove the users’ direct Office 365 Enterprise E3 assignments. The Microsoft Entra admin center’s Licenses blade supports managing and removing those direct license assignments at scale while preserving the group-inherited E5 licenses. Microsoft documents that directly assigned licenses can be removed without affecting inherited licenses.

**Learn more:** [Scenarios, limitations, and known issues for groups that manage licensing in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-group-advanced) · [PowerShell examples for group-based licensing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-powershell-graph-examples)

questions.question:
You must resolve the issue with guest-user invitations.  
  
What should you do in the Azure AD tenant?

options.text: Configure the Continuous access evaluation settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID external collaboration settings control who can invite B2B guest users and can allow or block invitations for specified external domains. These settings therefore govern guest-user invitation issues.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure external collaboration settings for B2B in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure)

questions.question:
You must resolve the issue with guest-user invitations.  
  
What should you do in the Azure AD tenant?
questions.explanation:
The review frequency is part of an access package’s lifecycle and recurring access-review configuration in Microsoft Entra entitlement management. The Identity Governance Administrator role can manage access packages and their access-review settings, and is the appropriate least-privileged choice among the listed roles.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Manage the lifecycle of group-based licenses in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-group-licenses) · [Deploying policies for governing access to applications integrated with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/identity-governance-applications-deploy)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that uses Microsoft Entra Permissions Management. Sub1 includes a user named User1. User1 has been granted multiple permissions throughout Sub1.  
  
You need to replace every permission granted to User1 with read-only permissions. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do from the Remediation tab in Permissions Management?

options.text: From the Role/Policy Template subtab, create a template.
From the My Requests subtab, create a new request.
From the Roles/Policies subtab, create a role.
From the Permissions subtab, use a quick action.

questions.explanation: A quick action on the Permissions subtab directly remediates and right-sizes an identity’s existing permission assignments, allowing the permissions to be replaced with read-only access with minimal administrative work. Creating a role, policy template, or access request requires additional configuration and does not directly remediate the existing assignments.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant containing the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713086620-zbck34er.png)  
  
You add an enterprise application named App1 and configure these **Self-service** settings:  
  
- **Allow users to request access to this application:** Yes  
- **To which group should assigned users be added:** Group1  
- **Require approval before granting access to this application:** Yes  
- **Who is allowed to approve access to this application:** User2  
  
Which users can request access to App1?
questions.explanation:
Self-service application access requests add approved users to the configured assignment group. A user who is already a member of that group already receives the application assignment and does not need to request access. Approval authority is separate from eligibility to submit a request, so User2 and User3 can request access.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra self-service application access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/manage-self-service-access)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual machine named VM1 and an Azure key vault named Vault1. VM1 has a system-assigned managed identity.  
  
You need to ensure that VM1 can retrieve the values of secrets stored in Vault1. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure the Resource access settings for Vault1.
Configure the permissions model for Vault1.
Add a user-assigned managed identity to VM1.
Assign an Azure role to VM1.

questions.explanation:
A system-assigned managed identity can be granted Key Vault data-plane access through Azure RBAC. Azure role assignments work only when the vault uses the Azure RBAC permission model, so that model must be configured before assigning VM1 a secrets-reading role, such as Key Vault Secrets User. Key Vault resource access settings govern network access rather than secret authorization.

**Learn more:** [Provide access to Key Vault keys, certificates, and secrets with Azure role-based access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-guide) · [Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) vs. access policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-access-policy)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Conditional Access policies.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Conditional Access cannot immediately act on an on-premises Active Directory account disablement that has not yet synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft Entra Connect Sync normally synchronizes directory changes on a 30-minute schedule, so this configuration does not satisfy the requirement for immediate prevention of authentication.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: Scheduler](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sync-feature-scheduler)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Azure AD Password Protection.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation: Azure AD Password Protection prevents users from choosing weak or banned passwords. It does not immediately disable the corresponding Azure AD account or revoke its ability to authenticate when the on-premises Active Directory account is disabled.

questions.question:
Solution: You configure password writeback.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Password writeback synchronizes cloud password changes or resets back to on-premises AD DS; it does not immediately disable a cloud identity when the corresponding on-premises account is disabled. The cloud account and access are disabled at the next Microsoft Entra Connect synchronization interval, which defaults to every 30 minutes.\
\
**Learn more:** [Self-service password reset FAQ - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/passwords-faq) · [How does self-service password reset writeback work in Microsoft Entra ID?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-sspr-writeback)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure pass-through authentication.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication validates user credentials directly against on-premises Active Directory during sign-in. An Active Directory account that has been disabled therefore cannot pass validation, immediately enforcing the on-premises disabled-account state for new authentications.\
\
**Learn more:** [Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/choose-ad-authn) · [Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication: Technical deep dive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-pta-how-it-works)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Conditional Access policies.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Conditional Access evaluates cloud sign-in conditions; it does not immediately propagate or enforce an on-premises Active Directory disabled-account state in Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft documents that password hash synchronization does not immediately enforce on-premises account-state changes, including account disablement, so this configuration cannot guarantee immediate prevention of authentication.\
\
**Learn more:** [Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/choose-ad-authn)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
In Microsoft Entra ID, you configure terms of use.  
  
You need to ensure that only users who accept the terms of use can access resources in the tenant. All other users must be denied access.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Terms and conditions in Microsoft Intune
an access policy in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
a conditional access policy in Microsoft Entra ID
a compliance policy in Microsoft Intune

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra terms of use are enforced through a Conditional Access policy that requires acceptance as a grant control for the targeted users and resources. A user who declines the terms of use is blocked from accessing the application.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up Microsoft Entra terms of use with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/terms-of-use)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must synchronize the ADatum users. The solution must satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Azure Active Directory Connect wizard, select Customize synchronization options.
From the Microsoft Azure Active Directory Connect wizard, select Change user sign-in.

questions.explanation:
`Start-ADSyncSyncCycle` triggers a Microsoft Entra Connect synchronization cycle, allowing directory changes for the users to be synchronized immediately. `Set-ADSyncScheduler` configures the scheduler rather than initiating a synchronization cycle.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect: ADSync PowerShell Reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/reference-connect-adsync) · [Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: Scheduler](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sync-feature-scheduler)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Exchange organization that uses the SMTP address space `contoso.com`.  
  
Several users use their `contoso.com` email address to self-service sign up for Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
You obtain global administrator privileges for the Azure AD tenant that contains the self-signed users.  
  
You need to stop users from creating user accounts in the `contoso.com` Azure AD tenant through self-service sign-up for Microsoft 365 services.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation:
`Set-MsolCompanySettings` configures the legacy tenant-wide self-service controls, including whether email-verified users can join the organization and whether users can create email-based self-service subscriptions. Disabling the applicable setting prevents creation of self-service accounts for the verified `contoso.com` domain. Current Microsoft Entra documentation describes the equivalent tenant-wide controls as `allowEmailVerifiedUsersToJoinOrganization` and `allowedToSignUpEmailBasedSubscriptions`.

**Learn more:** [Self-service sign-up for email-verified users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/directory-self-service-signup)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713800898-6cfpsj2t.png)  
  
Admin4 creates a Conditional Access policy named Policy1 by using the **Require multifactor authentication for Azure management** template.  
  
Which users will be required to use multi-factor authentication (MFA) the next time that they sign in?
questions.explanation:
Conditional Access template policies that target users automatically exclude only the user who creates the policy. The Azure management MFA template therefore requires MFA for Admin1, Admin2, and Admin3, while excluding Admin4, the policy creator.

**Learn more:** [Conditional Access templates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policy-common) · [Require MFA for Azure management with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-old-require-mfa-azure-mgmt)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that includes the users shown in the following table.

You have an administrative unit named Au1. Group1, User2, and User3 are members of Au1.  
  
User5 is assigned the User administrator role for Au1.  
  
For which users can User5 reset passwords?
questions.explanation:
A User Administrator assigned at an administrative-unit scope can reset passwords only for users who are direct members of that administrative unit. Adding Group1 to Au1 scopes management of the group itself, not management of Group1’s individual members. Therefore, User5 can reset the passwords of the directly assigned users User2 and User3.

**Learn more:** [Administrative units in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/administrative-units) · [Add users, groups, or devices to an administrative unit](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/admin-units-members-add)

questions.question:

What should you do?

options.text: Enable password hash synchronization in Azure AD Connect.
Configure an authentication method policy in Azure AD.
Enable federation with PingFederate in Azure AD Connect.

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure AD tenant containing the users shown in the following table.

A company policy prevents changes to user permissions.  
  
Which user can create appointments in every user's calendar at the company?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Graph `Calendars.ReadWrite` as an application permission allows an app to create, read, update, and delete events in all calendars without a signed-in user. User2 uses App2, which has that application permission. `Calendars.Read` permits only reading calendar data, and Azure AD administrative roles do not by themselves grant calendar write access.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
Users grant third-party cloud apps access to their data.  
  
You need to configure an alert that triggers when an app requires high permissions and has been authorized by more than 20 users.  
  
Which policy type should you create in the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal?
questions.explanation:
OAuth app policies monitor OAuth applications based on their requested permissions and the users who authorized them. They can generate alerts for apps that require a high permission level and exceed a specified authorization-count threshold.

**Learn more:** [Create policies to control OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/app-permission-policy) · [Investigate and remediate risky OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/investigate-risky-oauth)

options.text: Create a guest user account in contoso.com.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration creates a guest user in the resource tenant while allowing the external user to sign in with their own existing credentials. That guest user can be assigned access to an enterprise application such as App1.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft Entra tenant that includes a user named User1.

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.

Which risk detection type is categorized as a user risk?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD threat intelligence is a user risk detection because it identifies user activity that is unusual for the user or aligns with known attack patterns, using Microsoft’s internal and external threat intelligence. Impossible travel, anonymous IP address, and malicious IP address are sign-in risk detections.\
\

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription linked to a Microsoft Entra tenant. That tenant includes a registered app named App1.  
  
You have a partner organization with a Microsoft Entra tenant. That tenant includes a registered app named App2.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 can access App2.  
  
Which two credential types can App1 use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra registered application acting as a confidential client can authenticate with either a client certificate or a client secret to obtain an application token for a protected resource. These credentials are configured on the app registration and support client-credentials authentication across tenants when the target tenant grants the required consent and permissions.

**Learn more:** [Add and manage application credentials in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/how-to-add-credentials) · [Microsoft identity platform application authentication certificate credentials](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/certificate-credentials)

You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You deploy a new enterprise application named App1.  
  
When users try to give App1 access to the tenant, the attempt fails.  
  
You need to ensure that users can request admin consent for App1. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Enable admin consent requests for the tenant.
Designate a reviewer of admin consent requests for the tenant.
From the Permissions settings of App1, grant App1 admin consent for the tenant.
Create a Conditional Access policy for App1.

questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Entra admin consent workflow allows users who cannot consent to an application to submit an admin-consent request. Enabling admin consent requests activates that workflow; reviewers can then be configured to evaluate requests without granting App1 tenant-wide consent in advance.

**Learn more:** [Configure the admin consent workflow - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-admin-consent-workflow)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1.  
  
You purchase a Microsoft Entra Permissions Management license.  
  
You need to onboard Permissions Management.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Implement a Microsoft Entra application proxy.
From Microsoft Entra Permissions Management, configure data collection.
Create a role assignment for Sub1.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure the Diagnostic settings.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create an app registration.
From the Azure portal, create a data collection rule (DCR).

questions.explanation:
Azure onboarding in Microsoft Entra Permissions Management requires creating an Azure data-collector configuration and granting the Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management application the Reader role at the subscription or management-group scope. The role assignment supplies the access needed to read and collect authorization data from Sub1.

**Learn more:** [Onboard a Microsoft Azure subscription in Permissions Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/entra/permissions-management/onboard-azure)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes users running Microsoft Outlook 2016 and Outlook 2013 clients.  
  
You need to implement tenant restrictions while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure the Outlook 2013 clients to use modern authentication.
Upgrade the Outlook 2013 clients to Outlook 2016.
From the Exchange admin center, configure Organization Sharing.
Upgrade all the Outlook clients to Outlook 2019.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 thick clients, including Outlook, can enforce tenant restrictions only when they use modern authentication. Outlook 2013 supports modern authentication but does not have it enabled by default, so enabling it on those clients is the required first action and avoids unnecessary client upgrades.

**Learn more:** [Use tenant restrictions to manage access to SaaS apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/tenant-restrictions) · [Modern Authentication configuration requirements for transition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/exchange/administration/modern-authentication-configuration)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can create access reviews for Azure AD roles. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
Creating access reviews for Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) roles in Privileged Identity Management requires at least the Privileged Role Administrator role. User Access Administrator is relevant to access reviews of Azure resource roles, not Microsoft Entra roles.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an access review of Azure resource and Microsoft Entra roles in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-create-roles-and-resource-roles-review)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can create access reviews for Azure AD roles. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
Review frequency is configured as part of an access package assignment policy’s access-review lifecycle settings. In the Azure AD role model applicable to this scenario, the User Administrator role provides the required ability to manage that setting with less privilege than broader administrative roles; the other listed roles govern security, privileged role assignments, or external identity providers rather than access-package review configuration.

**Learn more:** [Create an access review of an access package in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-access-reviews-create) · [Delegation and roles in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-delegate)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a user named User1 and an Azure key vault named Vault1.  
  
You must ensure that User1 can read the metadata of certificates, keys, and secrets stored in Vault1. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should be assigned to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Key Vault Reader role permits reading metadata for a key vault and its certificates, keys, and secrets, but does not allow access to sensitive values such as secret contents or key material. This provides exactly the required read-only metadata access with least privilege.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles for Security - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/security) · [Provide access to Key Vault keys, certificates, and secrets with Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-guide)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to use Azure Monitor to analyze Microsoft Entra sign-in logs.  
  
You need to configure Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings.  
  
Which destination should be configured for the sign-in logs?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra sign-in logs must be sent to a Log Analytics workspace to integrate them with Azure Monitor Logs, where they can be queried and analyzed. Microsoft’s configuration guidance specifies selecting **Send to Log Analytics workspace** for this integration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Integrate Microsoft Entra logs with Azure Monitor logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-integrate-activity-logs-with-azure-monitor-logs)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant containing a user named User1 and a registered app named App1.  
  
User1 deletes App1's app registration.  
  
You need to restore the app registration.  
  
What is the maximum number of days after deletion in which you can restore the app registration?
questions.explanation:
A deleted application registration remains in a soft-deleted, restorable state for 30 days. After the 30-day window, the registration cannot be restored because it is permanently deleted.\
\
**Learn more:** [Restore or remove a recently deleted application with the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-restore-app)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709617945-x2msgb15.png)  
  
You configure a naming policy for groups in the tenant.  
  
Which users are affected by the naming policy?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 group naming policies exempt Global Administrators and User Administrators. Groups Administrators are permitted to configure naming policies but are not among the exempt roles, and users with no listed administrative role are also subject to the policy.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enforce a naming policy on Microsoft 365 groups in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-naming-policy)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709617945-x2msgb15.png)  
  
You configure a naming policy for groups in the tenant.  
  
Which users are affected by the naming policy?
questions.explanation:
Group-based assignment to an enterprise application in Microsoft Entra ID is supported only for security groups and for Microsoft 365 groups that have their SecurityEnabled property set to true; distribution lists and other unsupported group types cannot be assigned. Group1, a security group, and Group3, a Microsoft 365 group, both meet this requirement, whereas the other listed groups do not.

**Learn more:** [Manage users and groups assignment to an application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/assign-user-or-group-access-portal)

You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that includes a virtual machine named VM1.  
  
You need to enable Microsoft Entra sign-in for VM1 and configure VM1 to access resources in Sub1.  
  
Which identity type should be assigned to VM1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra sign-in on an Azure VM requires a system-assigned managed identity before installing the Microsoft Entra sign-in VM extension. That identity is tied to VM1 and can be granted Azure RBAC roles for resources in Sub1, allowing the VM workload to obtain Microsoft Entra tokens and access authorized resources.

**Learn more:** [Sign in to a Windows virtual machine in Azure by using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-windows) · [Managed identities for Azure resources overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription linked to a Microsoft Entra tenant. The tenant includes the groups shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713996243-el3b5grc.png)  
  
Which groups can be managed by using Privileged Identity Management (PIM)?
questions.explanation:
PIM for Groups can manage just-in-time membership or ownership for any Microsoft Entra security group or Microsoft 365 group, including both role-assignable and non-role-assignable groups. Only dynamic-membership groups and groups synchronized from on-premises environments are excluded; no such limitation is shown for any of the four groups. [Microsoft Learn: PIM for Groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/concept-pim-for-groups)

**Learn more:** [Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for Groups - Microsoft Entra ID Governance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/concept-pim-for-groups)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 2,500 users assigned individual Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses.  
  
From the **Groups** blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center, you assign Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E5 licenses to a group that contains all users.  
  
You need to remove the Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses from the users with the least administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Licenses blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center
the Administrative units blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra group-based licensing adds the E5 entitlement through group membership but does not remove an existing direct E3 assignment. The Licenses blade provides centralized license-assignment management, including unassigning licenses, making it the appropriate low-administration method for removing the direct E3 assignments at scale.

**Learn more:** [Assign or unassign licenses to a group in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/manage-group-licenses?view=o365-worldwide) · [Group-based licensing PowerShell examples](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-powershell-graph-examples)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with these settings:  
  
- Require users to register when signing in: Yes  
- Number of methods required to reset: 1  
  
Which authentication method is available to users?
questions.explanation:
A mobile app code is a supported SSPR authentication method. When one method is required for password reset, the mobile-app option available is a verification code.\
\
**Learn more:** [How Microsoft Entra self-service password reset works](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-sspr-howitworks) · [Enable Microsoft Entra self-service password reset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/tutorial-enable-sspr)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to create a Conditional Access policy that uses a Global Secure Access security profile. The solution must prevent users from accessing websites whose URLs contain the word `gambling`.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a web content filtering policy.

questions.explanation:
Global Secure Access security profiles contain linked web content filtering policies, and those profiles can be assigned through Conditional Access. A web content filtering policy provides URL-based filtering rules, so it must be created before it can be linked to the security profile that Conditional Access uses.\
\
**Learn more:** [How to configure Global Secure Access web content filtering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-configure-web-content-filtering)

You have an Azure AD tenant that includes the external user shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709834963-3ip3xabb.png)  
  
You update the user's email address.  
  
You need to ensure that the user can authenticate by using the updated email address.  
  
What should you do for the user?
questions.explanation:
For a Microsoft Entra B2B guest to sign in with a different email address, the guest’s redemption status must be reset after the email is updated. The user can then redeem the new invitation and use the new email address to sign in, without changing the existing guest object, group memberships, or app assignments.

**Learn more:** [Reset the redemption status for a guest user in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/reset-redemption-status)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708881337-laf27f1z.png)  
  
You create a dynamic user group and configure the following rule syntax.  
  
```text  
user.usageLocation -in ["US","AU"] -and (user.department -eq "Sales") -and -not (user.jobTitle -eq "Manager") –or (user. jobTitle -eq "SalesRep")  
```  
  
Which users will be added to the group?
questions.explanation:
Dynamic membership rules evaluate comparison operators before `-not`, `-and`, and `-or`. The rule therefore includes a user who is in US or AU, is in Sales, and is not a Manager, or any user whose job title is SalesRep. User1 meets the first condition, and User2 meets the SalesRep condition; User3 does not meet either condition.

**Learn more:** [Manage rules for dynamic membership groups in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/entra/identity/users/groups-dynamic-membership)

You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with these settings:  
  
- Require users to register when signing in: Yes

Which authentication method is valid for users?

options.text: an email to an address outside your organization

questions.explanation:
For SSPR configurations that require one authentication method, a mobile authenticator app can be used through its verification code. Push notification approval is available for the mobile-app method only when two reset methods are required.\

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) with these settings:  
  
- Require users to register when signing in: Yes  
- Number of methods required to reset: 1  
  
Which authentication method is valid for users?
questions.explanation:
SharePoint app-enforced restrictions limit unmanaged devices to browser-only access. Managed devices retain full access. An Azure AD-joined device and a compliant registered device are treated as managed for this control, so User1 and User2 have full access. Device3 is neither joined nor compliant, so User3 is restricted to limited web-only access.

**Learn more:** [Control access from unmanaged devices - SharePoint in Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/control-access-from-unmanaged-devices) · [Use application enforced restrictions for unmanaged devices - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-app-enforced-restrictions)

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You configure self-service password reset (SSPR) using these settings:  
  
- Require users to register when signing in: Yes  
- Number of methods required to reset: 1  
  
Which authentication method is valid for users to use?

options.text: an email to an address outside your organization
an email to an address in your organization

questions.explanation: For Microsoft Entra SSPR, email verification uses an alternate email address outside the organization so that the user can receive the reset verification message independently of the organizational account being recovered. With one verification method required, that external email address can satisfy the reset requirement.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a resource group named RG1 and four users named User1, User2, User3, and User4.  
  
You plan to assign the following roles to the users for RG1:  
  
- User1: Reader  
- User2: Contributor  
- User3: Storage Blob Data Reader  
- User4: Virtual Machine Contributor  
  
You are assessing the use of attribute-based access control (ABAC).  
  
Which user's role supports the use of ABAC?
questions.explanation:
Azure ABAC role-assignment conditions can be added to built-in or custom roles that have supported Blob Storage or Queue Storage data actions. Storage Blob Data Reader is explicitly a supported built-in role, so the role assigned to User3 supports ABAC.

**Learn more:** [Add or edit Azure role assignment conditions using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/conditions-role-assignments-portal) · [What is Azure attribute-based access control (Azure ABAC)?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/conditions-overview)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that contains the groups shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706494928-o5r30ydx.png)  
  
For which groups can you create an access review?

options.text: Group1, Group2, Group4, and Group5 only
Group1, Group2, Group3, Group4 and Group5

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra access reviews support assigned-membership security groups and Microsoft 365 groups. Dynamic groups are excluded from group access reviews because their memberships are determined automatically by membership rules. Therefore, Group1 and Group4 are eligible.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an access review of groups and applications in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review)
