options.text: a conditional access policy in Azure AD
a compliance policy in Microsoft Intune
an OAuth policy in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
an application control profile in Microsoft Intune

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Conditional Access policy can block legacy authentication requests, including Basic authentication, to Exchange Online. Blocking those requests restricts access to clients that support Modern authentication.

**Learn more:** [Block legacy authentication with Conditional Access - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-block-legacy-authentication) · [Disable Basic authentication in Exchange Online](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/disable-basic-authentication-in-exchange-online)

questions.question:
You need to assign licenses to ADatum's new users. The solution must satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
Which type of object should you create?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra group-based licensing can assign product licenses to members of a security group. A dynamic user security group evaluates user attributes against a membership rule and automatically adds matching users, allowing those users to receive the group’s assigned licenses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Assign Microsoft 365 licenses to user accounts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/assign-licenses-to-user-accounts?view=o365-worldwide) · [Create or update a dynamic membership group in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-create-rule)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
The company has a call center with 300 users. The call-center users share desktop computers and may use a different computer each day. The call-center computers are **not** configured for biometric identification.  
  
Users are not allowed to have a mobile phone in the call center.  
  
You need to require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for the call-center users when they access Microsoft 365 services.  
  
What should the solution include?
questions.explanation:
FIDO2 security keys are portable, device-bound hardware authenticators that users can carry between shared computers. They provide strong authentication through possession of the key plus a local user-verification gesture such as a PIN, so they do not require a mobile phone or biometric capability on the shared desktop. Microsoft specifically identifies FIDO2 security keys as an alternative authentication option for shared-device scenarios.

**Learn more:** [Passkeys (FIDO2) authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2) · [Passwordless for Students - M365 Education](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/education/guide/1-reference/protect-passwordless-students)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant containing two users named User1 and User2.  
  
You plan to take the following actions:  
  
- Create a group named Group1.  
- Add User1 and User2 to Group1.  
- Assign Azure AD roles to Group1.  
  
You need to create Group1.  
  
Which two settings can you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Group type: Security -Membership type: Dynamic User
Group type: Microsoft 365 -Membership type: Dynamic User
Group type: Security -Membership type: Dynamic Device

questions.explanation: Groups used for Azure AD role assignments must have Assigned membership (not Dynamic) and can be either Security groups or Microsoft 365 groups; the role-assignable flag must be set at group creation.

questions.question:
You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) P1 tenant.  
  
You need to review the Azure AD sign-in logs to investigate sign-ins that took place in the past.  
  
How long does Azure AD retain events in the sign-in logs?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID P1 retains sign-in activity logs for 30 days by default. Retaining sign-in data beyond that period requires routing or archiving the logs to another storage or analytics solution.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra data retention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/reference-reports-data-retention)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that uses Microsoft Entra ID Premium licenses.  
  
You plan to configure Terms of Use (ToU) for the tenant.  
  
You need to upload the ToU document.  
  
Which document format should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Terms of Use policies require a Terms of Use document in PDF format for upload.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set Up Microsoft Entra Terms of Use with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/terms-of-use)

questions.question:
You create a Log Analytics workspace.  
  
You need to implement the technical requirements for auditing.  
  
What should you configure in Azure AD?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD diagnostic settings select the activity logs to collect and send them to a Log Analytics workspace for auditing and analysis. Company branding, External Identities, and app registrations do not configure audit-log routing.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings for activity logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-configure-diagnostic-settings) · [Integrate Microsoft Entra logs with Azure Monitor logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-integrate-activity-logs-with-azure-monitor-logs)

questions.question:
You create a Log Analytics workspace.  
  
You need to implement the technical requirements for auditing.  
  
What should you configure in Azure AD?
questions.explanation:
Email one-time passcodes are used to authenticate a B2B guest when that guest redeems an invitation or accesses a shared resource. User2 is the new external recipient who has not previously accessed fabrikam.com resources, so this recipient requires the email passcode flow. User1 is already a guest in the tenant, and User3 is an internal fabrikam.com user; neither requires a new emailed passcode for this sharing action.

**Learn more:** [Email one-time passcode authentication for B2B guest users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/one-time-passcode) · [Microsoft Entra B2B integration for SharePoint and OneDrive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/sharepoint-azureb2b-integration)

questions.question:
You have a management group named Group1 that includes two Azure subscriptions, Sub1 and Sub2. The subscriptions are linked to a Microsoft Entra tenant containing a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can onboard Sub1 to Permissions Management. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which permission should you grant User1?
questions.explanation: Granting Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write at the Sub1 subscription scope allows User1 to onboard only that subscription; a management group scope would violate least privilege by including Sub2.

questions.question:
You have a management group named Group1 that includes two Azure subscriptions, Sub1 and Sub2. The subscriptions are linked to a Microsoft Entra tenant containing a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can onboard Sub1 to Permissions Management. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which permission should you grant User1?

options.text: the Groups blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center
the Identity Governance blade in the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
Group-based licensing does not automatically remove licenses assigned directly to users. Direct license assignments must be removed from the user accounts, and a PowerShell bulk operation is the lowest-effort method at this scale. Microsoft documents removing unnecessary direct licenses when users inherit licensing through a group; the current Microsoft Graph equivalent is `Set-MgUserLicense`.

**Learn more:** [PowerShell examples for group-based licensing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-powershell-graph-examples) · [Remove Microsoft 365 licenses from user accounts with PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/remove-licenses-from-user-accounts-with-microsoft-365-powershell?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure multi-stage attack detection to satisfy the monitoring requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Customize the Microsoft Sentinel rule logic.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel’s Fusion engine detects advanced multistage attacks by correlating signals from multiple products and data sources into high-fidelity incidents. Adding the appropriate Microsoft Sentinel data connectors makes those source signals available for this detection. The Fusion rule logic is hidden and cannot be customized; workbooks are for visualization and playbooks are for automated response. 

**Learn more:** [Configure multistage attack detection (Fusion) rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/configure-fusion-rules) · [Threat detection in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/threat-detection)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Active Directory forest synchronized with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant. The tenant uses pass-through authentication.  
  
A corporate security policy specifies the following:  
  
- Domain controllers must never communicate directly with the internet.  
- Only required software must be installed on servers.  
  
The Active Directory domain contains the on-premises servers shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783707275762-7ipwkit2.png)  
  
You need to ensure that users can authenticate to Azure AD if a server fails.  
  
On which server should you install an additional pass-through authentication agent?
questions.explanation:
For high availability, an additional standalone pass-through authentication agent should run on a server other than the Azure AD Connect server. Authentication agents require outbound Internet access, so installing one on either domain controller would violate the security policy. The unassigned member server can host the required additional agent without installing unnecessary software on a domain controller.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication: Quickstart](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-pta-quick-start) · [Microsoft Entra hybrid identity authentication options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/choose-ad-authn)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Exchange organization that uses the `contoso.com` SMTP address space.  
  
Several users use their `contoso.com` email addresses to self-service sign up for Microsoft Entra.  
  
You obtain Global Administrator privileges in the Microsoft Entra tenant that contains the self-signed-up users.  
  
You need to stop users from creating user accounts in the `contoso.com` Microsoft Entra tenant through self-service sign-up for Microsoft 365 services.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra controls whether email-verified users can join a tenant, and whether users can sign up for email-based subscriptions, through the authorization policy. `Update-MgPolicyAuthorizationPolicy` updates that policy; setting the applicable self-service sign-up properties to `false` prevents creation of email-verified accounts through this process.

**Learn more:** [Self-service sign up for email-verified users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/directory-self-service-signup) · [Update authorizationPolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/authorizationpolicy-update?view=graph-rest-1.0)

Your on-premises network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain and a certification authority (CA) named CA1.  
  
You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You need to implement certificate-based authentication in Azure AD. The solution must ensure users can sign in using certificates issued by CA1. What should you do first?

options.text: Add CA1 as a Certificate Authority to the Microsoft Entra ID tenant.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra certificate-based authentication validates user certificates only when their issuing CA chain is configured as trusted in the tenant. Adding CA1 as a Certificate Authority establishes that trust; key vault, auto-enrollment, and Windows Hello for Business do not configure Azure AD to validate certificates issued by CA1.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to monitor application access assignments by using Identity Governance. The solution must satisfy the delegation requirements.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the User consent settings for the enterprise applications.
Modify the Admin consent requests settings for the enterprise applications.

questions.explanation:
A catalog is the entitlement-management container for resources and access packages, including applications. Delegated administration is scoped through catalog roles, such as catalog owner and access package manager, so creating the catalog establishes the scope in which application access can be managed and delegated.

**Learn more:** [Delegate access governance to catalog creators in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-delegate-catalog) · [Delegation and roles in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-delegate)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant containing the objects shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706526458-pkv0jwjg.png)  
  
Which objects can be added as eligible in Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for an Azure AD role?
questions.explanation:
User objects, including guest users, can be made eligible for Microsoft Entra ID roles in PIM. A managed identity is a service principal, and service principals cannot be assigned as eligible for Microsoft Entra roles in PIM; they can only receive time-limited active assignments.

**Learn more:** [Plan a Privileged Identity Management deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-deployment-plan) · [Assign Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-add-role-to-user)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and Conditional Access policies.  
  
You need to block access to cloud apps when a user is assessed as being high risk.  
  
Which policy type should you create in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps access policies provide real-time control over user access to cloud apps through Conditional Access App Control. They can block access for specific users and apps based on risk factors, whereas activity policies govern actions performed within apps.

**Learn more:** [Control cloud apps with policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/control-cloud-apps-with-policies) · [Create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps access policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/access-policy-aad)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You open the risk detections report.  
  
Which risk detection type is categorized as a user risk?
questions.explanation: Leaked credentials is a user-risk detection because it indicates that a user's credentials are known to have been exposed. Impossible travel, anonymous IP address, and atypical travel are sign-in-risk detections.

Your network includes an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named `contoso.com` and a web app named `WebApp1`. `WebApp1` uses Integrated Windows authentication.  
  
Remote users access `WebApp1` by establishing a VPN connection to the on-premises network and using the URL `https//webapp1.contoso.com`.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that synchronizes with `contoso.com`.  
  
You perform these actions:  
  
- Deploy Microsoft Entra Private Access.  
- Configure a connector group containing a connector named `Connector1`.  
  
You need to ensure that remote users can access `WebApp1` by using Microsoft Entra Private Access.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enroll the remote users’ devices in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Private Access requires an application segment to define the private resource destination, port, and protocol that the Global Secure Access client should route through the selected connector group. Defining the `webapp1.contoso.com` HTTPS endpoint as an application segment enables access to the private web app.

**Learn more:** [How to configure per-app access using Global Secure Access applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-configure-per-app-access)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You deploy a third-party web gateway named Gateway1.  
  
You need to integrate Gateway1 with Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure data automatically flows to Defender for Cloud Apps.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
Defender for Cloud Apps uses Cloud Discovery automatic log upload to receive traffic logs automatically from a firewall or proxy. Configuration begins by creating a matching data source for that gateway; the log collector is then configured and associated with the data source.

**Learn more:** [Configure automatic log upload using on-premises Docker on Linux](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/discovery-docker-ubuntu) · [Get started with Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/get-started)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
You discover that users are connecting to unsanctioned third-party apps.  
  
You need to automatically identify and block the use of unsanctioned apps that have a risk score of 5 or higher and generate more than 200 GB of daily traffic. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Defender portal, create an app governance policy.
Create an app discovery policy by using the New popular app template.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a Conditional Access policy.
Create an app discovery policy by using the New risky app template.

questions.explanation:
The **New risky app** app discovery policy template is intended to detect risky or noncompliant cloud app use. Its risk-score and daily-traffic conditions can be customized to the required values, and its governance action can tag matching apps as unsanctioned; access is then automatically blocked. Starting from this template minimizes the configuration effort.

**Learn more:** [Create cloud discovery policies in Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/policies-cloud-discovery) · [Defender for Cloud Apps policy templates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/policy-template-reference)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network contains an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain. The domain synchronizes with a Microsoft 365 subscription by using Microsoft Entra Connect Sync.  
  
You plan to create 300 new users. The user-account details are stored in a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet.  
  
You need to automate creation of the users. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- The users must be able to access resources in the Microsoft 365 subscription.  
- The users must be able to access resources on the on-premises network.  
- Administrative effort must be minimized.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlets should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
`New-ADUser` creates the required accounts in the on-premises AD DS domain, which enables access to on-premises resources. Microsoft Entra Connect Sync can synchronize those AD DS accounts to Microsoft 365. `Import-Csv` reads the user data as rows from a CSV export of the Excel spreadsheet, allowing bulk account creation with minimal administrative effort. Microsoft documents using `Import-Csv` together with `New-ADUser` to create multiple Active Directory user objects.

**Learn more:** [New-ADUser (ActiveDirectory)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/new-aduser?view=windowsserver2016-ps) · [Import-Csv (Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/import-csv?view=powershell-7.6)

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that includes a user named User1 and uses Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
At 08:00 on Tuesday, User1 requests activation of a Microsoft Entra role that requires approval.  
  
You need to determine when the request will be automatically deleted if an approver does **not** respond.  
  
What should you identify?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra PIM allows 24 hours for delegated approvers to approve a role-activation request. An unapproved request expires after that fixed period, so a request made at 08:00 on Tuesday is deleted at 08:00 on Wednesday.\
\
**Learn more:** [Approve or deny requests for Microsoft Entra roles in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-approval-workflow)

At 08:00 on Tuesday, User1 requests activation of a Microsoft Entra role that requires approval.  
  
You need to determine when the request will be automatically deleted if an approver does **not** respond.  
  
What should you identify?

options.text: From Diagnostic settings in the Microsoft Entra admin center, send the logs to a Log Analytics workspace.
From Diagnostic settings in the Microsoft Entra admin center, stream the logs to an Azure event hub.
From Diagnostic settings in the Microsoft Entra admin center, archive the logs to a storage account.
From the Azure portal, create a data collection rule (DCR).

questions.explanation:
The `SignInLogs` table is queried in a Log Analytics workspace after Microsoft Entra sign-in logs are sent there through Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings. Sending logs to an event hub is for streaming, archiving to a storage account is for retention, and a data collection rule is not needed to route Microsoft Entra activity logs to Log Analytics.

**Learn more:** [Configure a Log Analytics workspace and a custom workbook](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/tutorial-configure-log-analytics-workspace) · [Access activity logs in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-access-activity-logs)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785139303580-cqeurvaa.png)  
  
You need to implement a Conditional Access policy that requires remediation for risky users.  
  
Which users can create the policy?
questions.explanation:
Conditional Access Administrator and Security Administrator are supported roles for creating and managing Conditional Access policies. Authentication Administrator does not grant Conditional Access policy-creation permissions. Microsoft Entra ID P2 is required when using Identity Protection risk signals in Conditional Access policies.

**Learn more:** [Plan a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/plan-conditional-access) · [New-EntraConditionalAccessPolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.entra.signins/new-entraconditionalaccesspolicy?view=entra-powershell)
